s.bbc0ceb4af8535c2: The word means hung, as though the chain dangles with nothing above it. Al-Bukhari includes many mu'allaq reports in his Sahih, and scholars read them by their wording: those he states firmly, in the active form, are generally reliable and usually connected elsewhere in the book, while those he introduces with a passive form such as it is narrated are weaker. Ibn Hajar traced their full chains in a separate work.
s.b17ec2831e62f82d: Muallaq · Mualaq · Muallak · Muallaqat · Mu'allaqat · Taliq
s.1222ffae2801a814: The last two surahs of the Qur'an, al-Falaq and al-Nas, recited for protection.
s.ba2765578a654465: The Prophet peace be upon him said verses had been revealed the like of which had never been seen, and then recited these two, in Muslim. He blew into his hands with them and with al-Ikhlas before sleeping and wiped over his body, in Bukhari, and taught that reciting the three surahs morning and evening suffices a person against everything, in a report collected by Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi. They are the core of any ruqya, and a person says them over themselves without needing a specialist.
s.490f370f4209f9dd: Muawwidhatain · Muawwithatain · Muawwizatain · Muawwidhat · Al-Falaq · Surah Falaq
s.94b51ec77f936b0d: A chain missing two or more narrators in a row, a wider break than munqati'.
s.2512601e2aad51f0: The word suggests something troublesome and hard to solve. It is more serious than a single missing link, since a gap that size can hide an entire generation. When a later writer quotes the Prophet with no chain at all, the result is usually mu'dal in effect.
s.87aa42d21d06604c: Mudal · Muadal · Mudhal · Muadhal · Mu'adal · Mudal hadith
s.b42fa79301394699: A miracle given to a prophet as proof of prophethood, which his opponents are unable to match.
s.8609eebc775cba5e: The word means that which renders others powerless. The staff of Musa, the healing given to Isa, and the splitting of the moon are examples, and the standing miracle of Muhammad peace be upon him is the Qur'an itself. A mu'jizah is public, tied to a claim of prophethood, and impossible to imitate, and that is what separates it from a karamah.
s.0e9862496a1484d7: Mujiza · Mojiza · Muajiza · Mujizat · Moajiza · Mu'jiza
s.47f19b0e63471934: Neutral: neither rewarded nor blamed, permitted and left entirely to your choice.
s.2b83aa8a96993a08: Which colour you wear and what you eat for breakfast are mubah, and most of ordinary life sits inside this category. A mubah act can become worship through intention, since eating so as to have strength to pray is rewarded, and sleeping so as to rise for fajr is rewarded. This is where the maxim that matters are judged by their intentions does its quietest and most useful work.
s.67b735ce1a60dbc0: Mubaah · Mobah · Jayiz · Ibahah · Ibaha · Jaiz
s.267135db31ad2109: A partnership where one side provides capital and the other the work, sharing agreed profits.
s.aea346f4d438231e: Losses of money fall on the investor while the working partner loses his effort, unless he was negligent or broke the terms. Profit must be divided by a stated ratio and never as a fixed sum, since a guaranteed return would quietly turn the arrangement into an interest bearing loan. Musharakah is its sibling, in which both sides put in capital and share profit and loss by agreement. Both predate Islam and were confirmed rather than invented by it, and both underpin profit sharing accounts today.
s.a3b33eed637754fb: Mudaraba · Modaraba · Mudharabah · Muzarabah · Qirad · Shirkat
s.036b8621250cc157: A hadith with words inserted into it, usually a narrator's explanation that later sounded like the Prophet's speech.
s.31769157be349dad: Insertions happen in the text and, less often, in the chain. The usual sign is a phrase that explains an unfamiliar word, or that reads like a legal clause in the middle of plain speech. Scholars caught them by finding other versions where those same words appear separately as the narrator's own comment.
s.2b0ee3cafd1aaeac: Mudrej · Idraj · Mudraj hadith · Mudraj al-matn · Mudraj al-isnad · Interpolated hadith
s.445da29fd4a79b6d: A hadith narrated in versions that clash, with no way to prefer one over the other.
s.7dc815ecdfecfad6: The word describes something shaking, unsteady on its feet. If one version can be shown to be stronger, the problem disappears and the weaker is simply set aside; idtirab is declared only when the versions are of equal weight and cannot be reconciled. It is a rare verdict, and it makes the hadith weak.
s.d27396c04aea912e: Mudhtarib · Muztarib · Mudtarab · Mudtareb · Idtirab · Iztirab
s.4b8bb4f616d7ec08: The last stretch of the Qur'an, from about Surah Qaf to the end, made up of shorter surahs.
s.520c2b4bbc0befe9: The name means the frequently divided, because the basmalah separates its many short surahs so often. Scholars split it into long, middle and short sections, which is the language books of fiqh use when describing what to recite in each prayer. Where it begins is disputed: most say Surah Qaf, others say al-Hujurat.
s.29c8ed7e7cddb4f4: Al-Mufassal · Mufasal · Mufassall · Mufassal surahs · tiwal al-mufassal · awsat al-mufassal
s.1a34cbef33b51711: A scholar who writes or teaches tafsir, trained in Arabic, the readings, the Sunnah and the occasions.
s.90b38f28e17e300a: Classical scholars set a demanding bar here, since an error is an error about the speech of Allah. The one thing a mufassir may never do is state what a verse means on the strength of personal opinion alone. Any reader may reflect on the Qur'an; explaining it authoritatively to others is a trained job.
s.c53973b9ea88a703: Mufasir · Mufassirun · Mufassireen · Mufassirin · Mufassiroon · Quran commentator
s.d4ac037bb44fc8f9: A scholar of hadith who has studied the chains, the narrators and the defects, not merely read collections.
s.043d4a4641843c60: The ranks are informal but real. A talib is a student, a muhaddith works in the field, a hafiz has mastered a great number of chains, and titles like hujjah were given to a handful of men. Knowing many hadiths is not the same as being a muhaddith; the skill lies in judging them.
s.fe743144e8ed7416: Muhaddis · Muhadith · Muhaddithun · Muhaddithin · Muhaddithoon · Mohaddis
s.fbc905b51d9ba5b7: The Muslims who left Makkah for Madinah, leaving homes and property behind.
s.f18b2e9a47f00288: The singular is muhajir, one who cuts ties and moves. They arrived with nothing and the Qur'an praises them alongside the Ansar as the first and foremost. Emigration from Makkah specifically ended with the conquest, when the Prophet said there is no hijrah after the opening, but striving and intention remain. He also defined the muhajir in a wider sense: the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden.
s.b7d61af89ff343ae: Muhajireen · Muhajirin · Muhaajiroon · Muhajir · Emigrants · Mohajir
s.1d7eb03cd46a0fe2: Taking account of yourself: a regular, honest review of what you did and why.
s.33093f94edec34d2: The Qur'an tells each soul to look at what it has sent ahead for tomorrow (Qur'an 59:18), and a well known saying attributed to Umar ibn al-Khattab is to call yourselves to account before you are called to account. Scholars describe it as a short daily session rather than a long anxious one, done before the deed to check the intention and after it to check the result. It is a tool, and like any tool a scrupulous person can overuse it.
s.6f8703fcde90c592: Muhasaba · Mohasaba · Muhasabat al-nafs · Muhasabah al-nafs · Self-accounting · Self-examination
s.134968eb543137e9: The clear verses whose meaning is decisive, and the verses that can carry more than one meaning.
s.60a1b0abc8ce7bf9: The Qur'an draws the distinction itself, in Surah Al Imran, and warns against those who chase the ambiguous looking for discord. Muhkam verses are the backbone: the commands, the prohibitions, the plain statements. Mutashabih covers what is genuinely open to more than one reading, and matters of the unseen whose reality many scholars leave to Allah rather than forcing into a shape.
s.e963801b0c5dd021: Muhkam · Muhkamat · Mutashabih · Mutashabihat · Mutashaabih · Muhakam
s.73e81429738c20b3: The struggle against your own self: making yourself do the right thing when you do not want to.
s.f33444a49e47c56a: The Qur'an promises guidance to those who strive for His sake (Qur'an 29:69). Classical writers describe it as three moves: opposing the appetite, refusing the whisper, and putting the limbs through the act until it becomes a habit. The often quoted line about returning from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad was judged by hadith scholars to have no sound chain, which does not remove the idea itself, since sound texts state it in other words.
s.c67157a2f11ce2c8: Mujahada · Mujahadat al-nafs · Jihad al-nafs · Jihad an-nafs · Mojahada · Struggle against the self
s.24e61d5f585ff9d9: Two recorded styles: mujawwad is slow and ornamented for listening, murattal is even and plain.
s.52d30646957c3128: Mujawwad is the style of the great reciters at public gatherings, with long pauses and phrases repeated at different pitches. Murattal moves steadily from beginning to end and is what most people use for daily listening and for memorising. Both must obey the same tajwid; the difference is delivery, not rules.
s.6d113c316e9b9cff: Mujawwad · Mujawad · Mujawwid · Murattal · Muratal · Murattil
s.6dc832b7f02b7aa9: A person legally responsible: sane, and past the age of puberty.
s.aa65b8b83377b77a: The obligations of fiqh apply once both conditions are met, and the Prophet said the pen is lifted from three: the sleeper until he wakes, the child until he matures, and the one who has lost his mind until he recovers. Children are taught to pray at seven and firmly encouraged at ten, but what they do counts as voluntary and earns them reward without obligation. Puberty is judged by physical signs, or where none appear, by an age the schools commonly set around fifteen.
s.1ba9b150167215d6: Mukalaf · Mukallef · Taklif · Takleef · Baligh · Baaligh
s.e8b11e9bcbb904cd: The science of handling two sound hadiths that appear to contradict one another.
s.f1f96c6e796d712c: The order of work, as the hadith scholars and most jurists set it out, is: reconcile them if both can be true in different situations, then check whether one came later and replaced the other, then prefer the stronger if neither of those works, and finally suspend judgement. Hanafi jurists run the same steps in a different order, looking for abrogation before reconciliation. Al-Shafi'i wrote the earliest surviving book on this, and Ibn Qutaybah wrote a well known one answering critics of hadith. Most apparent contradictions dissolve once the setting of each report is known.
s.06f84f8a51dc8478: Mukhtalaf al-hadith · Ikhtilaf al-hadith · Mushkil al-hadith · Mukhtalif ul hadith · Contradictory hadith · Conflicting hadiths
s.d67a446bc5279429: The study of how verses and surahs connect, and why they sit in the order they do.
s.19b59ffc4771466a: It asks why one verse follows another, and how a surah opens and closes on the same note. Al-Biqa'i's Nazm ad-Durar is the largest classical work built entirely on this idea. Some early scholars were cautious about it, since the arrangement is a matter of revelation rather than an author ordering his chapters.
s.c050043828a2e3f2: Munasabat · Munasaba · Ilm al-Munasabat · Nazm · Nazm al-Quran · coherence of the Quran
s.1b441b724471096c: A weak narrator contradicts a reliable one, or reports alone something nobody else reports.
s.96c15dcd1aa836b7: The opposite is called ma'ruf, the known version. Definitions varied: earlier critics sometimes used munkar simply for a lone report from a weak narrator, with no contradiction involved. Note that munkar here is a technical grade for a report, unrelated to munkar meaning a wrong act, and unrelated to the angel of that name.
s.1fff12f56cde5e6f: Munker · Munkir · Munkar hadith · Nakarah · Denounced hadith · Rejected narration
s.faa2bc8352de6a41: The two angels who question a person in the grave about their Lord, their religion, and their prophet.
s.f302f151bfb5d293: They are named in a hadith reported by al-Tirmidhi, and the three questions appear in several sound narrations. The believer answers with certainty and the grave is widened for him; the one who lived heedless can only say that he heard people saying something and repeated it. This is the trial of the grave that the Prophet peace be upon him taught his companions to seek refuge from in every prayer.
s.84cdf5d589cd927f: Munkar · Nakir · Nakeer · Munkar wa Nakeer · Munkar Nakir · Angels of the grave
s.4f1c232f681da8c9: A chain with a break in it: a narrator missing somewhere in the middle.
s.8f5ff81711a8c791: The word means cut. It is the general term for a gap that is not at the start of the chain, not at the Companion's place at the end, and not two names deep, since each of those carries its own label. Any break makes a report weak, because the missing man is unknown and could be anyone at all.
s.806fb078c5663bde: Munqati · Munqate · Munkati · Munqata · Inqita · Broken chain
s.f8fa21f0e8b0f502: A sale at a disclosed cost plus markup, widely used in Islamic banking in place of lending.
s.21dc0762c8953758: In its classical form the seller states what the goods cost him and what profit he is adding, so the buyer knows both figures. Modern banks use it to finance purchases: the bank buys the asset, then sells it on to the customer at a higher price payable in instalments. Supporters point out that the bank takes real ownership and real risk in between; critics answer that the outcome tracks interest too closely, and the disagreement among scholars is genuine and unsettled.
s.a6a45d0c8eb7c876: Murabaha · Bai murabaha · Murabahat · Morabaha · Murabaha financing · cost plus sale
s.a81a98de1d3162fc: Revision of what you have memorised, the daily work that keeps the Qur'an from slipping away.
s.21383d879e40f03d: The Prophet compared memorised Qur'an to tethered camels: let go of the rope and they are gone. Traditional schools split the day into new memorisation, recent revision and old revision, called sabaq, sabqi and manzil in South Asian madrasas. Most people who lose their hifz lose it here rather than in the memorising.
s.01a2669bf0ed93d9: Muraja'a · Murajaah · Murajah · Muraja · Mudarasah · Dawr
s.149a77b9f26e772b: Living with the awareness that Allah sees you, at the moment you are acting.
s.3a720c19c2887b37: The Qur'an says He is nearer to a person than his jugular vein (Qur'an 50:16), and that He is ever a watcher over you (Qur'an 4:1). It is the practical side of ihsan as the Prophet peace be upon him defined it to Jibril: worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you, in Bukhari and Muslim. Muhasabah looks back at the deed. Muraqabah stands inside it.
s.c058b034f6a9a942: Muraqaba · Moraqaba · Muraqabat · Watchfulness · Mindfulness of Allah · Consciousness of Allah
s.5f0599f3d316f1ad: A Tabi'i quotes the Prophet directly, leaving out the Companion who actually heard it.
s.e3587528bf1f2ca2: The missing man is almost always a Companion, and Companions are held to be trustworthy, which is why the schools differ here rather than simply calling it weak. Hadith specialists generally class mursal as weak. In law, the Hanafis and Malikis accept it, al-Shafi'i accepts it only when another route supports it, and reports from Ahmad show acceptance with conditions. Later scholars also separated the mursal of the senior followers, which is stronger, from that of the juniors.
s.f24fcf7972d71b6f: Mursel · Morsal · Mursal hadith · Mursal hadeeth · Irsal · Mursalah
s.802944659c843cb7: The best dressed youth in Makkah who gave it up, taught Madinah Islam, and died at Uhud.
s.2f2fd1ab4b816c79: His mother had raised him in luxury and cut him off when he believed. After the first pledge at Aqabah the Prophet sent him alone to Madinah as teacher and reciter, and through him whole households of the Aws and Khazraj entered Islam before the Hijrah. He carried the banner at Uhud and was killed there. When they came to bury him they had only one short cloak: covering his head left his feet bare, and covering his feet left his head bare.
s.a16e6f976253cf6d: Musab ibn Umayr · Mus'ab · Musab bin Umair · Musab ibn Umair · Mosab · Musab al-Khayr
s.e4f0b67a9317ebd8: A collection arranged by legal topic that includes Companion and follower statements alongside hadith.
s.e6375d586ea6c2c2: The two great examples are the Musannaf of Abd al-Razzaq al-San'ani and that of Ibn Abi Shayba. They are enormous, and they are the main window onto what the earliest generations actually practised. Unlike a musnad, arranged by narrator, a musannaf is arranged by subject.
s.429ad867329bc655: Musanaf · Musannef · Musannafat · Musannaf Abd al-Razzaq · Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah · Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba
s.6ef573f0cf4d8bce: A physical copy of the Qur'an: the pages, ink and binding, as distinct from the revelation itself.
s.0d8b739b8b4cc589: The word comes from sahifah, a written sheet, so a mushaf is the sheets gathered between two covers. Muslims keep the distinction: the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, the mushaf is the object you can drop or tear. Worn out copies are not put in the bin; they are buried or burned in a clean place. Uthman burned the copies his standard edition replaced, and later scholars differ over which of the two is better.
s.1b43292e27649378: Mus'haf · Mus-haf · Moshaf · Mushef · Musshaf · Mushaf Sharif
s.11248f60eec3bffa: Either a hadith with a connected chain reaching the Prophet, or a book arranged by narrating Companion.
s.38b1d0be38b11420: As a grade, musnad usually means both connected and traced to the Prophet. As a book type, a musnad gathers everything narrated by each Companion under his name, which suits tracing a narrator but makes finding a topic awkward. The largest is the Musnad of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, which holds sound and weak material together and needs a critical edition to use well.
s.1de75a8525b32263: Musned · Masanid · Musnads · Musnad hadith · Musnad Ahmad · Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal
s.daa1d9509a89d466: Al-Hakim's supplement, gathering hadiths he judged to meet the standards of al-Bukhari and Muslim.
s.e6bb810d2c487303: A mustadrak is a book that makes up what an earlier author left out. Al-Hakim al-Naysaburi compiled his late in life and never finally revised it, and later scholars including al-Dhahabi found him lenient. A grading of sahih from al-Hakim alone is therefore treated as a starting point for checking rather than as a settled verdict.
s.15df22072587e505: Al-Mustadrak · Mustadrak al-Hakim · Mustadrek · Mustadrak ala al-Sahihayn · Al-Hakim · Hakim al-Naysaburi
s.a991b1a953c68523: Recommended: rewarded if done, with no blame for leaving it.
s.c490492a2739dfd4: It covers the great mass of good practice, from the voluntary prayers around the obligatory ones to greeting people first and using the siwak. Mustahabb, mandub, sunnah and nafl are used almost interchangeably, with fine distinctions between the schools. Nobody is called to account for missing a mustahabb, which is why it should never be pressed on another person as though it were fard.
s.35d047cbfd3b24fd: Mustahab · Mustahabbat · Mustahib · Mustehab · Musthahab · recommended
s.0f3539120536b6d8: Temporary marriage for a fixed term, permitted in Twelver Shia law and prohibited in Sunni law.
s.8cec52fa3d3faca0: Sunni scholars hold it was allowed early in Islam and then abolished by the Prophet, with reports placing the final prohibition at Khaybar or at the conquest of Makkah, and 'Umar's public ban is widely cited alongside them. Twelver Shia jurists hold the permission was never abrogated, and regulate mut'ah as a contract with a stated term and a stated dower. The same word has an unrelated sense in Sunni fiqh: a consolation payment made to a divorced wife.
s.b22bff34901e3c7e: Mutah · Muta · Mutaa · Mutah marriage · Muta marriage · Nikah mutah
s.e28d3189f7ecd8e7: A second chain supporting the first through the same Companion, showing a narrator was not alone.
s.798d5b08d4449866: If a hadith comes only through one shaky narrator, and then a second route turns up where somebody else narrates it from the same teacher, the doubt about that man's memory eases. A full mutaba'ah agrees from the narrator himself; a partial one joins the chain further up. When the support comes through a different Companion instead, it is called a shahid.
s.27651ec72f3f07c1: Mutabaah · Mutabaa · Mutaba'at · Mutabaat · Mutabi · Muttaba
s.9337095dbdeb1cff: A report carried at every stage by so many people that they could not all have agreed on a lie.
s.2e57d929f4e45b57: There is no fixed minimum number; what matters is that the crowd is wide enough and independent enough to rule out collusion. Two kinds are described: mutawatir in wording, where the same phrase comes through, and mutawatir in meaning, where many different reports converge on one point. The five daily prayers and the number of their units reach us this way, by continuous practice as much as by text, which is a stronger route than any single chain.
s.5f0901d6a37c4814: Mutawaatir · Mutewatir · Mutawatur · Mutawaatirah · Tawatur · Tawaatur
s.476058a90c8f39f7: Reported by both al-Bukhari and Muslim, which is the highest ordinary grade of authenticity.
s.43b9cd8ce88c892a: The phrase means agreed upon. In most books it refers to the two of them together, narrating through the same Companion. Some authors stretch it to include the Musnad of Ahmad as well, so it is worth checking what a particular writer means by it.
s.9886ab90e9d3488e: Muttafaq alaih · Muttafaqun alayh · Muttafaqun alayhi · Mutafaq alaih · Muttafaq alayhi · Agreed upon
s.22feddf2942460fc: A chain in which every narrator genuinely took the report from the one named before him.
s.7ed8e0dc35064f72: Also called mawsul. Connection is the first of the five conditions of soundness, and it is checked by comparing lifetimes, travels and known teachers. A chain can be perfectly connected and still weak, if one of the connected narrators is unreliable.
s.9419bc60cb59a576: Mutasil · Muttasel · Mawsul · Mawsool · Mausul · Connected chain
s.756735b8deb54b0a: Malik ibn Anas's early collection, mixing hadith with Companion practice and the settled custom of Madinah.
s.89d2efef3791b04d: The name suggests something made smooth, or well trodden. It is the earliest of these books to survive in wide use, and it is a law book as much as a hadith book: Malik records a report, then how the people of Madinah actually acted. Al-Shafi'i is quoted as calling it the soundest book on earth after the Book of Allah, a judgement made before the two Sahihs were compiled.
s.9f7f38d6bfabcc80: Al-Muwatta · Muwatta Malik · Muwatta of Imam Malik · Muwattaa · Muwatta' · Muatta
s.0c3d968295cc4a64: The open ground between Arafah and Mina where pilgrims spend the night of the tenth.
s.ae94582521a8ff2b: The Qur'an calls it al-Mash'ar al-Haram, the Sacred Monument. Pilgrims arrive after sunset, pray Maghrib and Isha together, sleep on the ground under the sky, and gather pebbles for the stoning. The weak, the elderly and those accompanying them may move on to Mina in the later part of the night, a concession the Prophet gave to his own family.
s.a635d37f9a46bcb5: Musdalifah · Muzdelife · Mudzalifah · Muzdalifa · Al-Mash'ar al-Haram · Mashar
s.3c2348a0c621866a: Maintenance: the husband's duty to provide housing, food and clothing for wife and children.
s.0337f7f6462ea8f4: The Qur'an sets the measure by means, telling a man of wealth to spend from his wealth and one whose provision is straitened to spend from what God has given him. It is owed regardless of the wife's own income, since whatever she owns or earns remains hers alone. It continues through the waiting period after a revocable divorce, and a father's duty to maintain his children does not end when the marriage does.
s.bac294c4a5dc1d12: Nafaqa · Nafqah · Nafakah · Nafaqat · Nafaka · Infaq
s.4e70bef5c7a3a61f: The self: the inner person that can command wrong, blame itself, or come to rest.
s.44b25bc9ca217a8b: The Qur'an describes it in three states: the soul that commands evil (Qur'an 12:53), the self reproaching soul (Qur'an 75:2), and the soul at peace, called back to its Lord well pleased (Qur'an 89:27-28). These are not three souls but one self in three conditions, and a person moves between them in a single day. Struggling with the nafs is ordinary religious life, not a sign that something has gone wrong.
s.eafa0f0b02ed24e1: Nefs · Nafis · Nafss · Nafse · The self · Ego
s.bfdfef12b55d8a68: A substance counted as ritually impure, which must be removed from body, clothes and prayer place.
s.964b34a952958707: Urine, faeces, blood, pork and wine are the agreed cases. Water removes najasah once the colour, taste and smell are gone. The schools differ over particular cases, such as dogs, and over how small a trace is overlooked. Najasah is about the substance; the state of a person needing wudu or ghusl is hadath, and the two are often confused.
s.e602a530fe39851e: Najasa · Najis · Nijasah · Najaasah · impurity · filth
s.8b7e24f553cadd13: Carrying words between people in a way that sets them against each other.
s.ee3bfa53fc4539a1: The Prophet peace be upon him said the one who carries tales will not enter Paradise, in Bukhari and Muslim, and he passed two graves whose occupants were being punished, one of them for namimah. The Qur'an condemns the one who goes about with slander (Qur'an 68:11). It differs from ghibah in its aim: ghibah damages a reputation, namimah damages a relationship.
s.134f29082f235eaa: Nameemah · Namima · Nemima · Nammam · Qattat · Tale-carrying
s.67d98900c02e435a: Sincere advice: wanting good for someone and telling them, privately and without an audience.
s.8e88ddb70d8db541: The Prophet peace be upon him said the religion is nasihah, and when asked to whom, said to Allah, to His Book, to His Messenger, to the leaders of the Muslims and to their common people, in Muslim. The word is wider than correction; it means genuine goodwill in what you say and in what you hold back. Classical scholars insisted that advice delivered in public is closer to shaming than to advising.
s.d79b98fb1bfbcfb1: Naseehah · Nasiha · Naseeha · Nasihat · Nasehat · Sincere advice
s.2ccf226d1c4b1067: Abrogation: a later ruling replacing an earlier one, the abrogating verse and the abrogated verse.
s.5d85aefb7cfe1199: The Qur'an raises the idea itself, and the clearest example is the change of qiblah from Jerusalem to the Kaaba. Early scholars listed hundreds of cases, often using the word loosely for any narrowing or qualifying of a general rule. Later scholars tightened the definition sharply, and Shah Waliullah held that only about five genuine cases remain; the count is still debated.
s.41d7868c28726d8a: Naskh · Nasikh · Mansukh · Naasikh · Mansookh · Nasikh wal Mansukh
s.64c4ceeb2f011eb5: Hypocrisy: showing belief outwardly while concealing disbelief, or acting against the faith one claims.
s.4ce55c2634e04630: The Qur'an gives the munafiqun a surah of their own and says the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire (Qur'an 4:145). Scholars distinguish nifaq of belief, which is disbelief in disguise, from nifaq of conduct: the well known signs of lying, breaking a promise, and betraying a trust, reported in Bukhari and Muslim. The second kind was taught as a mirror for the believer to check himself, not as a label to hand to others.
s.d7225ef1d4d7d343: Nifaaq · Nifak · Nefaq · Munafiq · Munaafiq · Munafiqun
s.4e79e784b072cdda: The Islamic marriage contract, formed by offer, acceptance, witnesses and a mahr.
s.17aeccae6d3372c8: The word means to join. Marriage in Islam is a contract rather than a sacrament, and consent is its foundation: the Prophet annulled a marriage a woman told him she had not agreed to. Requirements differ a little between schools: the majority require a wali to contract on the bride's behalf, while Hanafis allow an adult woman to contract her own. Marriage is strongly encouraged rather than obligatory, and celibacy as a religious discipline has no place in Islam.
s.fce46c8404f379e6: Nikkah · Nikaah · Nika · Nekah · Nikah ceremony · Zawaj
s.3c9968481ef734a2: The minimum amount of wealth a person must hold before zakat becomes due on it.
s.42d9664881bd41ba: It is set by the Prophet's rulings at about 85 grams of gold or about 595 grams of silver, with slightly different weights reported. Scholars differ over which standard to apply to cash: the silver figure is much lower, so it brings more people into zakat and gives more to the poor, while the gold figure sets a higher threshold and is widely used today. Below the nisab, no zakat is owed and nothing is blameworthy.
s.a5cb0e21d83aa067: Nisaab · Nissab · Nesab · Nisab threshold · zakat threshold · minimum for zakat
s.e415a61c68c9d652: The intention in the heart that turns an ordinary act into an act of worship.
s.1da0321be3ff45ad: Every act of worship needs a niyyah, and the Prophet said actions are only by intentions. It lives in the heart, so knowing which prayer you have stood up for is already the intention. The schools differ over whether saying it aloud helps: Shafi'is and Hanbalis allow it as an aid to focus, Malikis prefer it left unsaid, and none of them count the spoken words as the intention itself.
s.68f45c37a08d6d79: Niyya · Niyat · Niyyat · Neeyah · Niyah · Niyet
s.f0718737c2ec0aa9: Intention, which decides what an act legally is, not merely whether it is rewarded.
s.9f2f42fe4ff5e604: The Prophet said that actions are only by their intentions, and jurists turned this into the first of the great legal maxims: matters are judged by their objectives. It settles whether a wash is a bath or a wudu, whether money handed over is a gift, a loan or a repayment, and whether ambiguous words of divorce take effect. In worship the intention lives in the heart; in contracts what you say and do binds you as well, because other people have relied on it.
s.0a2fc61a5561b190: Niyyah · Niyya · Niyat · Niyyat · Neeyah · Niyah
s.e9508801fc06e1af: Prophethood: Allah choosing certain men to receive revelation and deliver it, ending with Muhammad, peace be upon him.
s.27a44d3539463437: The Qur'an names many prophets and says every nation was sent a warner. A rasul is usually described as one sent with a new law or to a rejecting people, and a nabi as one continuing a law already given, though scholars word the distinction in different ways. Prophets are protected in conveying the message, a quality called ismah. Muhammad peace be upon him is the seal of them, so no prophet comes after him (Qur'an 33:40).
s.fc815b96297ebc84: Nubuwwat · Nubuwah · Nubuwwa · Prophethood · Prophecy · Nabi
s.fd9b08f5f92603df: A nun carrying no vowel, or a tanwin ending, which triggers four tajwid rules depending on what follows.
s.eb38b421f9c87f8f: Tanwin is the doubled vowel sign at the end of a word, sounded as an n. The letter that comes next decides what happens to it: izhar, idgham, iqlab or ikhfa. This single family of rules is where nearly every beginner's tajwid course starts.
s.65da30d1ba3128a7: Noon sakinah · Noon saakin · Nun sakin · Noon sakin rules · Tanween · Tanwin
s.8d7d0bbcb47dc54a: Undoing magic with magic, which the Sunnah rejects, unlike undoing it with the Qur'an.
s.9606655c618e8cee: Asked about nushrah, the Prophet peace be upon him said it is from the work of Shaytan, in a report collected by Abu Dawud. Scholars read this as the pre-Islamic method of going to another practitioner to break a spell, and they distinguish it from ruqya with the Qur'an and lawful supplication, which is permitted and was done by the Companions. In practice this is the line between a healer who recites what you can hear and understand, and one who does not.
s.bff33163a300f459: Nashrah · Nushra · Nushrah shirkiyyah · Undoing sihr · Breaking magic · Counter magic
s.4d378a2f60c6bf0d: The sending down of the Qur'an: gradually, over roughly twenty three years, alongside real events.
s.6beb17be65e82b30: The first revelation was Iqra, in the cave of Hira, and the last verses came near the end of the Prophet's life. The Qur'an explains its own slow pace: it came in stages to steady the Prophet's heart. A well known report from Ibn Abbas adds an earlier stage, the whole Qur'an brought down to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr and then released piece by piece.
s.6551f5efab46fb21: Nuzul · Nuzool · Tanzil · Tanzeel · Inzal · Wahy
s.265e1fba805b8724: The descent of Isa near the end of time, to break the cross, kill the Dajjal, and rule with justice.
s.26926207e87b3ea9: The Qur'an says he was not killed and not crucified, but that Allah raised him (Qur'an 4:157-158), and calls him a sign of the Hour (Qur'an 43:61). The hadiths describe his descent, his prayer behind the leader of the Muslims, and his death and burial afterwards like any other human being. He returns as a follower of the final Prophet, not with a new religion.
s.de0f5ce2265e3004: Nuzool e Isa · Nuzul al-Masih · Descent of Isa · Return of Jesus · Second coming · Jesus returns
s.91738ce3b07a83e9: Allah's decree carried out: the partner word to qadr, though scholars differ over which term means which.
s.e333b20ae3548e4c: One common explanation is that qadr is the eternal measuring and qada is the putting into effect, while other scholars reverse the two. Either way, when the pair is used together they mean one thing: nothing reaches you from outside Allah's knowledge and will. In fiqh the same word means making up a missed prayer or fast, and it also means a judge's ruling, which are different uses of one root.
s.7e608b7d5b4824fb: Qadha · Qaza · Kaza · Qadaa · Qadhaa · Qadha wa Qadar
s.2d4bc3f27d8c3278: Performing an obligatory act of worship after its proper time has passed, to make it up.
s.6916797c9debcd5e: The Qur'an tells whoever is ill or travelling in Ramadan to fast the same number of other days, which is the clearest case of qada. Missed prayers are made up as soon as one is able, in order where practical, and there is no need to announce or dramatise it. Someone with years of missed prayers is usually advised to add a few to each day rather than attempt to clear them at once.
s.15c783bd1ffaff33: Qadha · Qaza · Kaza · Qadaa · Qada al-fawait · Qadha prayers
s.0a709f1525fdffc7: A judge in an Islamic court, whose ruling binds, unlike a mufti's opinion.
s.4aff229bacb5a0c1: Appointment as a qadi was treated as a heavy burden rather than an honour, and several of the great imams refused it outright. The office asks for knowledge, integrity and independence, and classical manuals warn a judge not to rule while angry, hungry or distracted. The instruction reported from the Prophet, not to decide between two people until you have heard from both, is quoted in nearly every book on the subject.
s.2fb5bc9ba95b697d: Qadhi · Kadi · Qazi · Kadhi · Qaadi · Kazi
s.551b4d32236c7438: Allah's decree: that He knows, wrote, willed and created all that happens, without forcing anyone to sin.
s.c9b0c44dd1cc593f: Scholars describe four levels to it: Allah's knowledge of everything, its writing in the Preserved Tablet, His will, and His creating it. The Qur'an says He created every thing in due measure (Qur'an 54:49), and the word itself carries measure rather than blind fate. Belief in qadr is the sixth article of faith in the hadith of Jibril. It does not remove your choice and it is not a reason to stop trying, which is why the Prophet peace be upon him answered a question about it by telling the man to act.
s.913439eb02f878b9: Qadar · Qadhar · Kadar · Qader · Taqdir · Taqdeer
s.c32edd598bd87217: The Pen, commanded to write the decree of everything that would happen until the Day of Judgement.
s.cbf9c16361986169: Allah swears by the pen and by what they write (Qur'an 68:1). A hadith in the collections of Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi reports that the first thing Allah created was the Pen, and He said to it write, and it wrote what would be until the Hour. The image is not ink and paper but a matter already settled, which is why the Prophet peace be upon him told Ibn Abbas that the pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.
s.c535600c0549201e: Al-Qalam · Qalem · Qalm · Qalam e Taqdeer · The Pen · Pen of destiny
s.9cfc80f8a4dc5b3e: The heart: in the Qur'an the seat of understanding and intention, not the organ alone.
s.0d9096917462c16b: The Qur'an speaks of a sound heart brought to Allah (Qur'an 26:89), of hearts that are sealed, and of hearts covered by rust from what they earned (Qur'an 83:14). The Prophet peace be upon him said there is a morsel of flesh in the body which, if it is sound, makes the whole body sound, and it is the heart, in Bukhari and Muslim. Classical writers describe it in three states: sound, sick, and dead. This is why the science of the heart is treated as a discipline and not a mood.
s.b4cbecef07cacf8d: Kalb · Qalp · Alb · Qulub · Heart · Sound heart
s.7fff4fcb9e94a74d: The slight bounce on five letters when they carry no vowel: qaf, taa, ba, jim and dal.
s.8cb99defb78ee265: Teachers gather them in the phrase qutbu jad. The bounce is small in the middle of a word and stronger when you stop on the letter at the end of a verse. It is a spring off the letter, not an added vowel, so no eh or uh sound should be heard after it.
s.eda6b0d8dac72612: Qalqala · Kalkala · Qalqla · Qalqalah letters · Qutb Jad · Qutbu Jadin
s.9beabf752cf4788b: Being satisfied with enough, so that what you do not have stops taking up room.
s.cf60d269d374f63b: The Prophet peace be upon him said a person has succeeded who submitted, was given just enough, and was made content by Allah with what He gave him, in Muslim. He also said richness is not having many possessions, but richness of the soul, in Bukhari and Muslim. Qana'ah is not a ban on ambition or on earning. It is the removal of the ache that no amount answers.
s.936201f261ec7e0c: Qanaah · Qana'a · Qanaat · Kanaat · Qanaa · Contentment
s.5985e3d22c11a074: A reciter of the Qur'an; in the classical sense, one trained and certified in a particular reading.
s.04672cae59331f2c: The plural is qurra, and in the earliest generations it meant the scholars who carried the Qur'an rather than performers. A muqri is a qari licensed to teach and to grant ijazah. Today the word is used loosely for anyone who recites beautifully, which is harmless, but the older meaning is worth keeping in view.
s.c433241ef7440d54: Qaari · Qare · Kari · Qari' · Qariah · Qaria
s.e71bf32bf2ee0fed: The jinn companion assigned to each person, whose work is whispering toward wrong.
s.a2aecfe9ee04d6fb: The Prophet peace be upon him said that every one of you has a companion from the jinn and a companion from the angels, in a report in Sahih Muslim, and said that his own had submitted so that it only urged him toward good. The Qur'an uses the same word for a companion who speaks up on the Day of Judgement (Qur'an 50:23-27). It is not a double of you, a shadow self, or a source of information about your life, and most of the popular material about it goes far beyond anything the texts say.
s.627443b95f99799b: Qareen · Kareen · Qarreen · Qarina · Hamzaad · Hamzad
s.e9deb05b1c100f51: Shortening the four-rak'ah prayers to two while travelling, and combining two prayers in one time.
s.41946e3579f4d833: The Qur'an mentions shortening prayer on a journey, and the Prophet did it consistently. Qasr applies to Dhuhr, Asr and Isha only; Fajr and Maghrib are never shortened. Jam' is a separate concession, joining Dhuhr with Asr or Maghrib with Isha. The schools set different thresholds for how far you must travel and how long you may stay before you pray in full again.
s.a3080bc86ad935ee: Qasar · Kasr · Qasr salah · shortening prayer · travel prayer · Jam
s.0d8f35c85afff896: Hardness of heart: the state in which reminders arrive and nothing moves.
s.f7582745ea31f8d7: The Qur'an says hearts hardened after that until they were like stones or harder (Qur'an 2:74), and warns those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah (Qur'an 39:22). Classical writers trace it to accumulated small sins, idle talk, overeating, and long neglect of remembrance. The prescription they give is unglamorous: return to the daily adhkar, sit with people who remember Allah, visit the sick, and give something away.
s.f9e51b05e6bc43f3: Qaswat al qalb · Qaswah · Qasawah · Rayn · Ran · Hard heart
s.05f9a34036952e06: Legal maxims: short principles that gather the pattern behind thousands of separate rulings.
s.ac2b30e854e17b9a: Five are counted as the great ones: matters are judged by their intentions; certainty is not lifted by doubt; hardship brings ease; harm is to be removed; and custom decides. They are teaching tools and aids to reasoning rather than sources in their own right, and every one of them has recognised exceptions. Al-Suyuti's al-Ashbah wa al-Naza'ir is the best known collection.
s.87ed384b7312c769: Qawaid fiqhiyyah · Qawaid · Qawa'id · Kawaid · Qaidah · Qaida fiqhiyya
s.19dd27753e0f2eab: The direction of the Kaaba in Makkah, which Muslims face when they pray.
s.83d59c3df708cba7: For sixteen or seventeen months in Madinah the Muslims prayed towards Jerusalem, and in the second year after the hijrah the Qur'an turned them to the Sacred Mosque. Those far from Makkah are asked for the direction rather than a perfect line, and someone with no way of knowing prays towards their best judgement and the prayer counts. Mosques mark it with a niche called the mihrab.
s.1db0762d09dc9133: Qibla · Kiblah · Kible · Qiblah direction · Kaaba direction · Qibla finder
s.4c781de9edaa91a3: The canonical ways of reciting the Qur'an, each carried by chain from the Prophet through a named reader.
s.a35aa6909b0776a2: Ten readings are accepted as authentic, each passed on by two main transmitters, giving twenty transmissions in common use. The differences are small and mostly touch vowels, lengthening or a single letter; they rarely change meaning, and where they do the two meanings sit alongside each other rather than clash. A reading counts as authentic only if it has a sound chain, fits the Uthmanic skeleton and is valid Arabic.
s.0cede56ed33c168c: Qiraat · Qira'aat · Qiraah · Qira'ah · Qiraa'at · Qirat
s.f8bac446c82ddcf8: Equal retaliation for murder or injury, which the victim's family may always waive for compensation.
s.4290b536d869ed98: The Qur'an calls it life for you, meaning that a known and strictly limited penalty restrains the endless blood feuds it replaced. It requires a court, proof and deliberate intent, and it is never a private act of revenge. The Qur'an then urges pardon and calls forgiving it an expiation for the one who forgives, and the family may accept diyah or waive everything, which classical practice treated as the better road.
s.dbb689d1d6aac32b: Qasas · Qisaas · Kisas · Qisas law · Qissas · retaliation
s.34015ccdd263c89f: The standing part of the prayer, where al-Fatihah and other verses are recited.
s.3b643e33e61f2cb1: Qiyam simply means standing. Standing is required in obligatory prayers for anyone able to do it; someone who cannot stand prays sitting, and someone who cannot sit prays lying down, with no loss of reward. The same word appears in qiyam al-layl, meaning standing in prayer through the night.
s.920b69f202697374: Qiyaam · Kiyam · Qiam · standing in prayer · Qiyam al-layl · Qiyamul layl
s.d6f079d1d72905eb: The Day of Resurrection, when this creation ends, the dead are raised, and everyone is judged.
s.390722064b128968: The word means the standing, because people stand before their Lord. Its timing is known to Allah alone, though the Prophet peace be upon him described signs that come before it. The Qur'an returns to this Day constantly, not to frighten, but because a life that ends in an account is lived differently from one that does not.
s.f2e30bbc1bda421e: Qiyamat · Qiyaamah · Qayamat · Kiyamet · Yawm al-Qiyamah · Judgement Day
s.3bf336e066d287b2: Analogy: extending a known ruling to a new case that shares the same underlying reason.
s.e303fa62adda6e80: The classic example is extending the prohibition of wine to every intoxicant, because the reason behind the ruling is intoxication rather than grapes. It has four parts: the original case, the new case, the ruling, and the 'illah or effective cause, and identifying the 'illah is the difficult part. All four Sunni schools accept qiyas as a source; the Zahiri school rejected it and worked from the texts alone.
s.d09dcd44ff83ab6a: Qiyaas · Kiyas · Qias · Qiyass · Kiyaas · analogy
s.72eaa19e3bc6e540: A supplication said standing in prayer, most often in witr or in times of crisis.
s.c18ef2265b04a800: The word means devout standing. The schools place it differently: Hanafis say it in witr all year, Shafi'is in the dawn prayer and in witr in the second half of Ramadan, Malikis in the dawn prayer, and Hanbalis in witr. Most also recognise qunut an-nazilah, a supplication added during public calamity. Its wording is not fixed, so a person may ask in their own words.
s.5f89fac831a7023e: Qunoot · Kunut · Qunut nazilah · Dua qunoot · Dua e qunoot · Qunut in witr
s.40333cd4743a443a: The speech of Allah revealed to Muhammad in Arabic over about twenty three years, preserved word for word.
s.78339f0009ece02a: The word means the recitation, from a root meaning to read aloud. It is one book of 114 surahs, revealed piece by piece between Makkah and Madinah, memorised by the Companions and written down in the Prophet's lifetime. Muslims hold that the Arabic wording is itself the revelation, which is why any rendering into another language is called a translation of the meaning and never the Qur'an.
s.5a62c7032a8b424d: Quran · Koran · Qoran · Kuran · Quraan · Al-Quran
s.a24effbd229c12cb: Milk kinship: breastfeeding in infancy creates the same marriage bars that birth creates.
s.af9ae84ec11bc608: The Qur'an names milk mothers and milk sisters among those a man may not marry, and the Prophet said that nursing forbids what birth forbids. The schools differ over how much is enough: Shafi'is and Hanbalis require five separate feeds, while Hanafis and Malikis count any amount that reaches the stomach. All agree it must fall within the nursing years, which the majority place in the first two.
s.828df861f445f103: Radaah · Rida · Ridaah · Radha · Rada · Radaa
s.7af01d525f3d800c: Mercy: the disposition to spare, relieve and be gentle, in Allah first and in people after.
s.c1a2a1b9a3069077: The Qur'an says His mercy encompasses all things (Qur'an 7:156), and that the Prophet peace be upon him was sent as a mercy to the worlds (Qur'an 21:107). He said the merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful, and told his companions to be merciful to those on earth so that the One in the heaven would be merciful to them, in a report collected by Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi. Rahmah in a person is not softness of opinion. It is the reflex to relieve someone when you could have walked past.
s.b02b52b7fd7fbc81: Rahma · Rahmat · Rehmat · Marhamah · Rahman · Raheem
s.32dbb9e26fc1c094: Hope in Allah's mercy, held by someone who is still working, not by someone who has stopped.
s.65304b5697802504: The Qur'an forbids despair of Allah's mercy and says He forgives all sins (Qur'an 39:53). Scholars separate raja' from wishful thinking, tamanni: hope plants and then expects a crop, wishing expects a crop with no seed. A common counsel is to keep fear slightly ahead while a person is in health, and to keep hope ahead when death is near.
s.479679642afcb4aa: Raja · Rajaa · Rajaa' · Radja · Hope · Hope in Allah
s.fd7756b79e23b149: One complete unit of prayer: a standing, a bowing, and two prostrations.
s.01bd4f3694b5a98c: Prayers are counted in rak'ahs. Fajr is two, Maghrib is three, and Dhuhr, Asr and Isha are four each. Within one rak'ah you stand and recite, bow, rise, prostrate, sit, and prostrate again. The plural is raka'at, which is why you will hear both forms.
s.bacdd68d5cdb8a8f: Rakah · Raka · Rakat · Rakaat · Rakaah · Rakka
s.cde84e10894698de: The spelling of the Uthmanic copies, kept in mushafs even where it differs from modern Arabic spelling.
s.22e337f751decab5: The original copies carried no dots and no vowel marks, only the consonantal skeleton, which could hold more than one authentic reading at once. Later scholars added dots, vowels and stop marks without touching that skeleton. This is why some words are written in the mushaf differently from how they are written today, and why Uthmani and simplified Indo-Pak printings look unlike each other on the page.
s.c0e492a7a48722d9: Rasm al-Uthmani · Rasmul Uthmani · Rasm · Uthmani script · Usmani script · Uthmani mushaf
s.971cc40c910eba06: The space in the Prophet's Mosque between his house and his pulpit, called a garden of Paradise.
s.f4a111beb7ba6230: The Prophet said that what lies between his house and his minbar is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. It is marked today by a green carpet where the rest of the mosque is red. Scholars read the saying two ways: that the ground itself is literally of Paradise, or that worship performed there leads to Paradise. Either way it is a place to pray in, not to touch, and crowding others out of it is not piety.
s.8b99dca8e6c687f6: Rawda · Rauda · Rawza · Riyad ul Jannah · Riyadh al-Jannah · Roza
s.18af05cdf417be83: A narrator: one of the people in the chain who heard a report and passed it on.
s.f1c4974079eab6a6: Every rawi in a chain has a file. Scholars recorded when he was born, who he studied with, how good his memory was, whether he was honest, and whether he lived long enough to have met the man he quotes. A hadith is only as strong as the weakest rawi in its chain.
s.71905b30d9aa8292: Raawi · Rawee · Ravi · Ruwat · Ruwaat · Narrator
s.3322f408cd8a289a: Interest or unjust increase on a loan or exchange, forbidden in the Qur'an in severe terms.
s.555f486ad124f240: Two forms are named: riba al-fadl, an unequal swap of the same commodity hand to hand, and riba al-nasi'ah, the increase charged for time, which is what an interest bearing loan involves. The Qur'an permits trade and forbids riba in the same breath, and the objection is to money multiplying from money with no shared risk and no real goods. Scholars differ sharply over how far the ruling extends into modern banking, and Islamic finance is the attempt to answer that.
s.13cde9a9edf23e3f: Ribaa · Sood · Reba · Ribba · Riba al-fadl · Riba al-nasiah
s.affe91498a9c88cb: Contentment with what Allah decrees, so the heart stops arguing with what already happened.
s.88c52d99867f536f: The word means to be pleased, and it runs both ways: Allah pleased with the believer and the believer pleased with Him (Qur'an 98:8). Scholars distinguish it from sabr, which holds steady under a blow, while rida no longer wishes the blow away. It applies to what has already been decreed. It does not mean accepting oppression, and it does not stop anyone from seeking a remedy.
s.a064275bdc565919: Ridha · Ridaa · Riza · Reza · Raza · Radiya
s.5ea5f6f3152fb679: Apostasy: abandoning Islam after having accepted it.
s.447843d43b44aa9e: Classical law treated open apostasy as a capital offence, drawing on prophetic reports rather than on the Qur'an, which mentions apostasy several times without prescribing any worldly penalty and states plainly that there is no compulsion in religion. Hanafis did not apply the death penalty to a woman who apostatised, and jurists across the schools required that repentance be invited first. Many contemporary scholars read the classical rulings as addressing public treason within a specific political order rather than private belief, and the question is actively debated.
s.f6b4f461831203c7: Ridda · Irtidad · Murtad · Murtadd · Riddat · Irtidaad
s.98b7424b743d54f5: The act of transmitting a report, and the version transmitted; its partner science is dirayah, understanding it.
s.25afd48cdadd18f2: Ilm al-riwayah is the work of carrying reports accurately. Ilm al-dirayah is the work of judging and understanding them. A person can be excellent at one and poor at the other, which is why some famous narrators were not jurists and some great jurists narrated little.
s.5ef3eb5ea8b86590: Riwaya · Riwaayah · Riwayat · Rivayat · Riwaayat · Narration
s.14040e1e94af1fe0: Narrating a hadith in one's own words while keeping its meaning, rather than the exact wording.
s.f10237e081d1cb6a: This is why the same event appears with different phrasing in different books. The majority allowed it for someone who knows Arabic precisely and understands what the words are doing, while a strict minority insisted on the wording as heard. Certain texts were held back from it, such as the supplications the Prophet taught word for word.
s.fa2ae136f248fcf8: Riwaya bil mana · Riwayah bil ma'na · Riwaya bil-mana · Riwayah bilmana · Naql bil mana · Narration by meaning
s.61be07b319c4a5c1: Performing worship so that people will see it, which empties the act of its reward.
s.c590e2532470bec5: The word comes from seeing, and its close cousin sum'ah is doing something so that people will hear of it. The Qur'an condemns those who pray only to be seen (Qur'an 107:6), and the Prophet peace be upon him called showing off the lesser shirk, in a report from Imam Ahmad. Being pleased that someone noticed a good deed is not riya. Riya is when being noticed was the reason you did it.
s.74375c758c2e2423: Riya · Riyaa · Riaa · Ria · Riyaa' · Showing off
s.b7b038f3e232f9f9: Al-Nawawi's topical collection on character and worship, the hadith book most widely read by ordinary Muslims.
s.7b2beebf00114275: The title means the gardens of the righteous. He drew almost entirely on the well known collections, opened each chapter with verses of the Qur'an, and arranged the whole book around how a person should live rather than around legal chapters. A small number of its reports are weak, and modern critical editions mark these.
s.f0925bfbc07ed765: Riyad us Saliheen · Riyadh as-Salihin · Riyadus Salihin · Riyad as Salihin · Riyaad as-Saaliheen · Riyad al-Saliheen
s.027a6d702b79bbca: The belief that the people of Paradise will see their Lord with their eyes, after death.
s.0816d6412d1289bf: The Qur'an says that on that Day some faces will be radiant, looking at their Lord (Qur'an 75:22-23), and sound hadiths compare the sight to seeing the full moon without crowding. Sunni Islam affirms this sight in the next life while denying that anyone sees Allah in this one. The Mu'tazila denied it altogether, and Twelver Shia theology also generally rejects a literal vision.
s.bb3e31533f37d4b9: Ruyatullah · Ruyat Allah · Ruyah · Rooyat · Seeing Allah · Seeing God in Paradise
s.6176df70ae188bfe: A quarter of a hizb, shown by the small ornamental star in the margin of the mushaf.
s.2d6ba1cee99bbd28: There are 240 of these quarters, four to each of the sixty hizbs. The symbol is a printer's mark added by later scholars so readers can keep their place and portion out a daily amount. It carries no ruling; nothing is said or done when you reach one.
s.b011614a13920e60: Rub al Hizb · Rubu al hizb · Ruba al-Hizb · quarter hizb · flower symbol in the Quran · star symbol Quran
s.9f65f312465f9f14: The spirit that gives a body life, whose reality Allah kept to Himself.
s.80ad1cef7c28a971: When the Prophet peace be upon him was asked about the ruh, the answer came: say, the spirit is from the affair of my Lord, and you have been given only a little knowledge (Qur'an 17:85). It is taken at death, held in the barzakh, and returned to the body at the resurrection. Many scholars use ruh and nafs for the same thing seen from two angles, while others treat them as distinct.
s.d5ee585db1f678eb: Rooh · Ruuh · Rouh · Ar-Ruh · Roh · Spirit
s.756826862e211f04: A concession: permission to do the easier thing when a recognised excuse applies.
s.546e7533c5bd935d: Shortening prayer while travelling, breaking the fast when ill, and wiping over socks are all rukhsah. The Qur'an states plainly that God intends ease for you and does not intend hardship, and the Prophet is reported to have said God loves His concessions to be taken as He loves His commands to be obeyed. Taking a concession you genuinely qualify for is not weakness, and refusing one out of scruple is not extra piety.
s.4d806e28cec03482: Rukhsa · Rukhsat · Rukhas · Ruhsat · Rukhsah shar'iyyah · concession
s.9d98055c70e6b8de: The bowing in prayer, hands on the knees, back level, praising Allah's greatness.
s.b5475b8501234cdb: From the standing position you bow with the back straight and the hands resting on the knees, saying subhana rabbiyal azim, glory to my Lord the Magnificent. The Qur'an repeatedly commands the believers to bow, and the posture is one of the pillars of the prayer without which a rak'ah does not count.
s.eff449fa42e98dc0: Ruku · Rukoo · Rukuu · Rukua · Roku · bowing
s.38b2a8e63982f034: A short thematic passage marked with a small ain in the margin, mostly in South Asian mushafs.
s.0a8aa1b102559ae7: The word is the same one used for bowing in prayer, because an imam would recite one such passage and then bow. It groups a handful of verses that hang together, which makes it a natural unit for tarawih and for memorising. It is a later reading aid and is absent from most Arab printings.
s.5204e596245c9f58: Ruku · Rukoo · Rukuu · Ruku Quran · Ashara · ayn symbol Quran
s.393ee6c45e60a3ae: Reciting Qur'an and prophetic supplications over a sick or afflicted person as treatment.
s.3d17915743f24a55: The Qur'an calls itself a healing for what is in the chests (Qur'an 10:57). The Prophet peace be upon him permitted ruqya so long as it contains no shirk, in Muslim, and approved a Companion who recited al-Fatihah over a man who had been stung, in Bukhari and Muslim. Anyone may recite over themselves or their family; no special person is required. Large fees, secret formulas, unintelligible words, and requests for the patient's mother's name are all signs to walk away.
s.1299bea8a9c90342: Ruqyah · Rukya · Roqya · Ruqia · Ruqyah shariah · Ruqya shariyyah
s.b33cb0b5f99b579b: Walking seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwah, beginning at Safa and ending at Marwah.
s.f6366a91d01487db: It retraces Hajar's search for water for her infant son Isma'il, which ended with the spring of Zamzam. Each single crossing counts as one, so the seventh brings you to Marwah. The Qur'an names the two hills among the symbols of Allah. Men jog lightly between the two green markers, where the valley floor once lay; women walk throughout.
s.b692ec9518382257: Sai · Saee · Saiy · Sa'ee · Say · Safa and Marwa
s.bde79dd7a9afea7d: Holding yourself steady under what is hard, without complaint to creation and without giving up.
s.5df8ad9a540dde90: The root means to restrain or to confine. Scholars usually give it three fields: steadiness in obeying Allah, steadiness in staying away from what He forbade, and steadiness under what He decrees. The Qur'an pairs it with prayer as the two things to seek help by (Qur'an 2:153). It does not mean feeling nothing: the Prophet peace be upon him wept when his son died and said the eye weeps and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord, in Bukhari.
s.21bb954fcf55d7a9: Sabar · Saber · Sabir · Sabrun · Sabr jameel · Sabr-e-jameel
s.75e223c78f95a4cd: Voluntary giving, of any amount and at any time, to anyone in need.
s.ff3dd7fbe81896e9: The root is sidq, truthfulness, because giving is treated as proof that a claim to faith is real. Unlike zakat it has no threshold, no fixed rate and no fixed recipients. The Prophet counted removing harm from a path, a good word, and a smile as sadaqah, so it is not limited to money. Giving quietly is described in the Qur'an as better than giving openly.
s.4f60567855e4292a: Sadaqa · Sadqah · Sadakah · Sadaka · Sadqa · Saddaqah
s.f560c7e7763d67d5: A charity that keeps benefiting people, so its reward continues after the giver dies.
s.d07f244bc26ddd15: Jariyah means flowing. The Prophet said that when a person dies their deeds stop except for three, and named ongoing charity, knowledge that others benefit from, and a righteous child who prays for them. A well, a tree, a school and a copy of the Qur'an left for others are the classic examples. Endowing property permanently for this purpose is called waqf.
s.da1baf280ab6b4ba: Sadaqa jariya · Sadqa jariya · Sadaqah jaria · ongoing charity · continuous charity · Waqf
s.94edcec703a09f55: The phrase Allah the Magnificent has spoken the truth, often said on finishing a recitation.
s.4f3cadef35589ac9: The words are true in themselves and echo a phrase in Surah Al Imran. What scholars differ over is treating them as a fixed ending that must always follow recitation, since neither the Prophet nor the early generations are known to have made a habit of it. Some call it a harmless custom, others discourage making it a rule; leaving it out is not a fault.
s.efd02e3efb2d5380: Sadaqallahul Azeem · Sadaqa Allahu al-Adheem · Sadaqallah · Sadakallahul azim · Sadaqallahul Azim · saying after reciting Quran
s.ba4e7012cb87c3d0: Blocking the means: forbidding something lawful because it reliably leads to something forbidden.
s.18d207aa70a82890: The classic proof is the Qur'anic instruction not to insult what others call upon besides God, lest they insult God in return out of ignorance. Malikis and Hanbalis use the principle heavily, while Shafi'is and Hanafis apply it more sparingly, since without limits it can be stretched to forbid nearly anything. Its mirror image, opening the means, is used to encourage whatever leads to a required good.
s.574637202d4a26a6: Sadd al dharai · Sadd adh-dharai · Sad al-zarai · Sadd ul dharai · Dharia · Dhariah
s.ebeaa9cb4448fae5: Two small hills in Makkah, now enclosed in a corridor, walked between during hajj and umrah.
s.83b5a7e9f9f300b7: The Qur'an names them among the symbols of Allah. Hajar crossed the ground between them seven times searching for water for Isma'il, and pilgrims repeat her crossing in the rite called sa'i. Both hills are now inside the Sacred Mosque, in a long marble gallery called the mas'a, and only the bare rock at each end still shows. It is a mother's desperate search preserved as an act of worship.
s.5f9f1780f1640476: Safa Marwah · Safa and Marwa · Al-Safa wal-Marwah · Safa Marwa · Sufa and Marwah · Safaa Marwah
s.04c84621ebd0af6f: The Companions: anyone who met the Prophet as a believer and died still believing.
s.c3638e7409cb4932: The singular is sahabi. That definition is Ibn Hajar's, and it is deliberately wide, so a child lifted up to see him once counts alongside Abu Bakr. At the Farewell Pilgrimage the number present is traditionally given as more than a hundred thousand. Sunni scholarship holds them collectively upright in transmission, which is why hadith critics examine the chain from the generation after them onwards.
s.f2a5212340bee251: Sahaba · Sahabi · Sahaabah · Ashab · As-hab · Companions
s.0d03124aa171028c: The record of a person's deeds, handed to them on the Day of Judgement.
s.79a380e97fe1b273: The Qur'an says every person's record is fastened to them and will be brought out as a book found spread open, with the words: read your record, today you are sufficient as a reckoner against yourself (Qur'an 17:13-14). Elsewhere the wrongdoers say of it: what kind of book is this, it leaves out nothing small or large (Qur'an 18:49). Receiving it in the right hand is the sign of success.
s.26422bfa9b1bcee4: Sahifa · Sahaif · Suhuf · Kitab · Book of deeds · Record of deeds
s.2875813837949ada: The written charter the Prophet drew up on reaching Madinah, binding its tribes into one body.
s.1acef3195f7c8cf3: It made the Muhajirun and Ansar and the Jewish tribes of the city into a single political community for defence, fixed responsibility for blood money clan by clan, and stated that the Jews had their religion and the Muslims theirs. Disputes were to be referred to the Prophet. Its text is preserved in the sirah literature rather than in the hadith collections, and historians treat it as among the earliest documents of the Muslim community.
s.6293cc4e8b603138: Constitution of Madinah · Charter of Medina · Sahifah al-Madinah · Mithaq al-Madinah · Medina Charter · Dustur al-Madinah
s.71b398f3d365d405: A hadith that meets all five conditions of authenticity, with nothing missing and no hidden flaw.
s.6fb7f213a25d05cd: The five conditions are an unbroken chain, every narrator upright, every narrator accurate, no contradiction of stronger narrators, and no hidden defect. Sahih is a verdict about how safely the report reached us, not a claim that its wording is revealed like the Qur'an. A lower grade, sahih li-ghayrihi, is lifted to this level by supporting chains.
s.4679568356d6ba81: Saheeh · Sahi · Sahee · Sohih · Sahiih · Sahih hadith
s.cc681a1d38323dfb: The collection of Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari, held to be the soundest book after the Qur'an.
s.fb6dad9d2ecec8e7: Its full title describes it as a sifted, connected, authentic collection. Al-Bukhari arranged it by chapter, and his chapter headings carry his own legal conclusions, so the book argues as well as reports. He required proof that a narrator actually met the person he quotes, a stricter rule than Muslim's. Reports repeat across chapters because he cites one hadith in several places for several points, which is why the raw entry count is far larger than the number of distinct hadiths.
s.03adce190fb9cde3: Sahih Bukhari · Saheeh al-Bukhari · Bukhari · Bukhaari · Buhari · Al-Bukhari
s.d550efb99eb6a097: A hasan hadith lifted to sahih because it is reported through more than one chain.
s.d6ed452836917ae2: Sahih li-dhatihi is sound in itself, by a single strong chain. Sahih li-ghayrihi is sound because of what stands beside it. Both are acted upon, and books of takhrij often write only sahih without saying which of the two they mean.
s.09829c3f8b40f7bd: Sahih li ghayrihi · Saheeh li ghairihi · Sahih lighairihi · Sahih bi ghayrihi · Sahih due to others · Saheeh li ghayrih
s.f953aea4d0f557be: The collection of Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, second of the two Sahihs and the better organised of them.
s.163ed269feadc183: Muslim gathered all the chains of a hadith in one place instead of scattering them, which makes his book easier to study. He held that narrators living in the same period with the possibility of meeting is enough, without proof of an actual meeting. His introduction is a short treatise on hadith method and is still read on its own.
s.974a0b583d556fae: Saheeh Muslim · Sahih ul Muslim · Muslim Sharif · Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj · Sahih al-Muslim · Shahih Muslim
s.7602e71e9d9ebc14: The two Sahihs, of al-Bukhari and Muslim, the most rigorously screened collections in Sunni Islam.
s.745fb532471936d4: Both authors set out to include only what they judged authentic, and these two books were received by the community with an acceptance given to no others. A small number of their reports were criticised by later specialists such as al-Daraqutni, and most of those criticisms concern a particular chain rather than the meaning of the text. Saying a hadith is in the Sahihayn normally ends the argument about its authenticity.
s.52df7e5e1616cf7c: Sahihain · Saheehain · As-Sahihayn · Saheehayn · The two Sahihs · Bukhari and Muslim
s.e1a7ab0de0c2e9af: The prostration made on reaching one of the Qur'an's marked verses of prostration, in prayer or outside it.
s.3c454897601f1ef1: The mushaf marks these verses in the margin, usually with the word sajdah and a line above the text. The schools count them differently, at eleven, fourteen or fifteen, so mushafs printed in different regions mark a different number of them. It is a single prostration, and most scholars hold it is recommended rather than required, including for someone who is only listening.
s.d2775f346bb77cb6: Sajda tilawat · Sajdah tilawat · Sujud at-tilawah · Sujood tilawah · Sajda e tilawat · Ayat as-Sajdah
s.32874f333f235739: Generosity: giving easily, before being asked, without making the receiver pay in dignity.
s.da3ef54ddfdf6053: The Qur'an says whoever is protected from the greed of his own soul, those are the successful (Qur'an 59:9), and the Prophet peace be upon him was described as the most generous of people, and most generous of all in Ramadan, in Bukhari and Muslim. Scholars place sakha' between two failures: miserliness on one side, wasteful display on the other. The measure in the Sunnah is what remains with you after the giving, not the size of what was given.
s.a5b19ee58969ceaf: Sakha · Sakhaa · Sakhawah · Karam · Jud · Generosity
s.40d789f8b5748b3a: A stillness Allah sends down into the heart, usually at the moment it is least expected.
s.3136002299c7da54: The Qur'an says He sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers (Qur'an 48:4), and describes it arriving in the cave when the Prophet peace be upon him told Abu Bakr not to grieve (Qur'an 9:40). It is spoken of as given rather than produced. It is not the same as being calm by temperament, and its absence in a hard moment is not a sign that a person has been abandoned.
s.5b86657096431e26: Sakina · Sakeena · Sekine · Sakinah in the heart · Tumaninah · Itminan
s.638cbc670812c0c9: A brief silence held without taking a breath, then the recitation carries straight on.
s.93fdd753fa054ee1: It keeps two words from running together in a way that could mislead the ear. In the Hafs reading there are four of them, in al-Kahf, Ya-Sin, al-Qiyamah and al-Mutaffifin, and the mushaf marks each with a small seen. Other readings place their pauses differently.
s.8e6296ea11f7d090: Sakta · Sakt · Saktah Hafs · Sakta in Quran · brief pause · silent pause
s.66cbbe886d594cc6: The first three generations of Muslims: the Companions, the Followers, and those after them.
s.5c6addf18392c4fb: The word means those who went ahead, the way a caravan sends people forward. Ahl as-Sunnah treat their shared understanding as the safest reading of the Qur'an and Sunnah, on the reasoning that people closest to the source heard the language as it was meant. The modern movement label Salafi is a separate and contested usage; belonging to the salaf is a matter of century, not of party.
s.31a45961e537729b: Salafi · Salafus Salih · Salaf as-Salih · Salafus saliheen · As-Salaf · Predecessors
s.35c9458e0a32d5e4: The formal Muslim prayer, performed five times a day at set times, facing Makkah.
s.6074d3a3be9563a5: The word means connection and supplication. Salah is a fixed sequence of standing, bowing, prostrating and sitting, with recitation from the Qur'an, done at five appointed times between dawn and night. It is the second pillar of Islam and the first act a person is asked about on the Day of Judgement. Persian and Urdu speakers usually call it namaz, which is the same thing.
s.8b5e8ba976726923: Salat · Salaah · Salaat · Sala · Namaz · Namaaz
s.cbc872cafe95e318: Soundness of the chest: carrying no grudge against anyone, whether or not they deserved one.
s.ffe039ded5432c0c: The Qur'an teaches the believers to pray that Allah leave no rancour in their hearts toward those who believed (Qur'an 59:10), and describes the people of Paradise as having every trace of it removed from their chests (Qur'an 7:43). In a report collected by Ahmad, a man was named as one of the people of Paradise, and the only practice found in him was that he went to sleep holding nothing against any Muslim. Forgiving the person is 'afw; salamat al-sadr is what remains in you afterwards.
s.bbe93a2d757ddf17: Salamat as-sadr · Salamatus sadr · Hiqd · Ghill · Ghil · Rancour
s.65cd0c12b11360e0: The two rak'ah prayer on the morning of the two Eids, with extra takbirs and a sermon after.
s.46dba2a7b66c861d: It is prayed in the mid-morning, in congregation, without adhan or iqamah, and the number of added takbirs differs by school. Rulings on it differ too: Hanafis call it wajib, Hanbalis a communal obligation, Shafi'is and Malikis a confirmed sunnah. Praying it in an open space rather than inside the mosque is the older practice.
s.de163e69a1de6a77: Eid prayer · Salatul Eid · Eid salah · Salat ul eid · Id prayer · Eid namaz
s.3c4169602fe30b1a: Two voluntary rak'ahs followed by a supplication asking Allah to choose the better of two paths.
s.ed3dbc752c4da303: The word means asking for the good. The Prophet taught it for ordinary decisions, and it is prayed once you already have an inclination, not instead of thinking and asking advice. A common misunderstanding is that it must produce a dream or a sign; it does not. You pray, you decide, and you trust the outcome you are given.
s.946420b571e58853: Istikhara · Istikhaarah · Istekhara · Estekhara · Isthikara · prayer for guidance
s.1944569e07d49ab8: The funeral prayer, said standing over the deceased, with no bowing and no prostration.
s.0038ee01048b40a3: It consists of four takbirs said while standing: al-Fatihah in the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools and praise of Allah in the Hanafi and Maliki, then salawat on the Prophet, then supplication for the deceased, then the closing salam. It is a communal obligation, meaning that if enough people pray it the duty is lifted from the rest. It is a prayer for the dead person, not a ceremony for the family, which is why it is kept short.
s.5270381c7363ef62: Janazah prayer · Janaza · Salatul janazah · funeral prayer · Namaz e janaza · Jenaze namazi
s.cd89234cf93ab96a: Asking Allah to honour the Prophet, usually in the words sall Allahu alayhi wa sallam.
s.3fd9d242475f3880: The Qur'an says Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet, and instructs the believers to do the same (Qur'an 33:56). He said, peace be upon him, that whoever sends one blessing upon him, Allah sends ten upon that person, in Muslim. The fullest wording is the one taught inside the tashahhud, known as the Ibrahimic form. Elaborate composed litanies of salawat circulate in some traditions, and scholars differ on using them in place of the narrated wording.
s.e1038ebd27d8afdf: Salawaat · Salat ala an-Nabi · Salatun Nabi · Durood · Darood · Durood Sharif
s.61a225826cdaa920: A Persian who searched through two religions for the truth and was enslaved before finding it.
s.3ebf60f8d30a602e: He left his father's fire worship for Christianity, served a succession of monks, and was told by the last of them that a prophet was about to appear in a land of date palms. On the way he was betrayed and sold as a slave into Madinah, where he recognised the signs he had been described. The Companions helped him buy his freedom. At the Trench it was his suggestion, unknown to the Arabs, that saved the city, and the Prophet is reported to have said Salman is of us, the people of the house.
s.81034a677bce7751: Salman the Persian · Salman Farsi · Salman al-Farsi · Selman-i Farisi · Salman e Farsi · Salman Pak
s.a71485a6c4abaad4: Receiving a hadith by hearing it directly from a teacher, the strongest of the ways to take a report.
s.ec2d5f736ae18d49: Scholars listed several ways of receiving hadith, in descending strength: hearing the teacher recite it, reading it back to him, a written licence, being handed a manuscript, correspondence, and finding a book with no licence at all. The wording of a chain tells you which way was used, so haddathana means he narrated to us in person, while akhbarana usually signals that it was read back to him.
s.4e0fd8da299b9b4c: Sama · Samaa · Samaah · Sima · Sema · Hearing
s.214712c19dd98f27: The chain itself, the line of narrators supporting a text, used almost interchangeably with isnad.
s.80706d1023f0eb66: The root means to lean something against a support. Strictly, sanad is the chain and isnad is the act of citing it, but in practice scholars use each word for the other. A strong sanad does not by itself make a strong hadith, because the text can still carry a hidden defect.
s.8b6c9ce5e0861a7f: Sened · Sanadd · Sanads · Asanid · Chain of narrators · Sanad hadith
s.01cd822216f1d84c: Fasting: abstaining from food, drink and intimacy from true dawn until sunset, with intention.
s.c97d453e5bd53d04: The word means to hold back. Fasting the month of Ramadan is the fourth pillar, and voluntary fasts are kept on other days through the year. The Qur'an sets its purpose as taqwa, God consciousness, and the Prophet warned that a fast without leaving off false speech is only hunger and thirst. Illness, travel, pregnancy, nursing, menstruation and old age all carry recognised concessions.
s.cb02b9d65ce5657c: Siyam · Saum · Soum · Roza · Rozah · Oruc
s.3a0199aa67088c40: An acceptable narrator contradicts someone stronger, so his version is set aside as odd.
s.c0d7613f926495a9: The point is not that the man is weak. It is that when a reliable narrator's version cannot stand beside the version of narrators who are more reliable or more numerous, one of the two must be a mistake. The stronger version is then called mahfuz, the preserved one. Freedom from shudhudh is one of the five conditions of a sahih hadith.
s.c11504235a3c2a01: Shadh · Shaadh · Shaz · Shazz · Shaadhdh · Shudhudh
s.82fc807994355613: Intercession: one person asking Allah on behalf of another, and only by Allah's permission.
s.7f41a3a08fc90f06: The Qur'an denies intercession that works like influence over a king, and affirms it with permission: who is there that can intercede with Him except by His leave (Qur'an 2:255). The greatest instance is the Maqam Mahmud, the praised station, where the Prophet peace be upon him asks for the standing to be relieved and the judgement to begin. Angels, prophets, martyrs and even a person's own children are described as interceding. Asking Allah to grant you the Prophet's intercession is agreed upon; addressing the deceased directly is where positions divide.
s.561437df2bba9e89: Shafaat · Shafa'at · Shafaa'ah · Shifaah · Shafaa · Intercession
s.456a0f50a965f4d6: The school of al-Shafi'i, known for tight textual method and a systematic theory of sources.
s.072dd8e35018aad1: Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i died in 204 AH and wrote the Risalah, the first surviving work of usul al-fiqh. His school prevails in Egypt, East Africa, Yemen, Kurdistan and much of Southeast Asia. It leans on hadith more readily than the Hanafis do, and it rejects istihsan as a source in its own right, holding that preference without evidence is lawmaking.
s.a8951b37367fe39d: Shafi · Shafii · Shafiee · Shafie · Safii · Syafii
s.8ba5a146ed6ccbd4: The testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His Messenger.
s.1216001031943016: It is the first of the five pillars and the door into Islam: whoever says it, understanding and meaning it, is a Muslim. It has two halves, which is why it is often called the shahadatain, the two testimonies. The first half empties the heart of every other object of worship; the second names the one man whose example shows how that worship is done. It is not a formula that works by sound. The scholars set conditions for it, among them knowledge of what it means, certainty rather than doubt, sincerity, truthfulness, love, acceptance and acting on it.
s.b3a750ae01a7d2c4: Shahada · Shahadatain · Kalima · Kalimah · Kalima Tayyiba · Kalimat at-Tawhid
s.67040058cb119dce: A supporting report of the same meaning narrated through a different Companion.
s.aea591583038c396: The word means witness. Where a mutaba'ah props up a particular narrator, a shahid props up the content itself from another direction. Several lightly weak reports with different Companions behind them can together raise a hadith to hasan li-ghayrihi, provided none of them is severely weak.
s.df703a9ea455e9e0: Shaahid · Shahed · Shawahid · Shawaahid · Shahid hadith · Witness narration
s.5c87535288321a5c: The opening of the chest: the settled ease Allah gives when a person is guided toward something.
