s.f5317f16bf8ff0b0: The Qur'an says whoever Allah wishes to guide, He opens his chest to Islam (Qur'an 6:125), and reminds the Prophet peace be upon him that his own chest was opened for him (Qur'an 94:1). This is the usual answer to what happens after salat al-istikharah: not a dream and not a sign, but a decision that stops feeling stuck, followed by acting on it. If no clarity comes, you consult, you weigh, you choose, and you trust the outcome you are given.
s.a0fb00f33cbca169: Sharh as-sadr · Sharh sadr · Sharhus sadr · Inshirah · Opening of the chest · Peace of mind
s.3ca6e3ddb33eaccf: The whole of what God revealed as guidance: belief, worship, character and law together.
s.24b906ece7934e52: The word literally means the path to water, and the Qur'an uses it for the way God set out for the Prophet to follow. It is far wider than law in the modern sense; most of it concerns prayer, fasting, honesty and family, and only a small portion concerns courts and punishment. Shari'ah is the revelation itself, while fiqh is the scholarly understanding of it, and collapsing the two makes human opinion sound divine.
s.666ae2235240021d: Sharia · Shariah · Sheria · Sharee'ah · Syariah · Seriat
s.eeb41e56012e1330: A devil: any rebellious jinn, and with the definite article, Iblis himself.
s.2b953067d70e21e5: The Qur'an says he is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy (Qur'an 35:6), and gives him only two tools, whispering and inviting. He cannot compel anyone; on the Day of Judgement he tells his own followers that he had no authority over them except that he called and they answered (Qur'an 14:22). The Qur'an also calls some human beings shayatin, so the word is not limited to jinn.
s.0c3ed6271fa712b1: Shaitan · Shaytaan · Shaitaan · Sheytan · Sheitan · Syaitan
s.bdfdb333accb25f9: The Makkan valley where the Prophet's clan was penned by a boycott for about three years.
s.6a44580bb86a19dd: Quraysh hung a written pact in the Ka'bah agreeing to no trade and no marriage with Banu Hashim until they surrendered him. Believer and unbeliever of the clan were shut in together, living on what sympathisers smuggled past the guards, and children's crying could be heard outside. It broke when several Quraysh who had never been comfortable with it tore the document up. Khadijah and Abu Talib both died soon after, in what is called the Year of Sorrow.
s.cb42f42d63fd341f: Shib Abi Talib · Shiab Abi Talib · Valley of Abu Talib · The Boycott · Social boycott of Banu Hashim · Shi'b Bani Hashim
s.6ac6fdcb67d8a189: Giving to something other than Allah what belongs to Allah alone, above all worship.
s.b4dcc7ae6e401bd8: The word means to make a partner or to share. The Qur'an says Allah does not forgive that a partner be set up with Him, and forgives what is less than that for whom He wills (Qur'an 4:48). Commentators read that of the one who dies without repenting, since the Qur'an elsewhere promises forgiveness to whoever turns back. Scholars distinguish major shirk, which takes a person outside Islam, from minor shirk, which is a grave sin but does not.
s.dbe67a0e7ec34a8c: Shrik · Sherk · Shirek · Schirk · Associating partners with God · Polytheism
s.fd9fd8b09169f90e: Minor shirk: acts like showing off in worship, which damage sincerity without putting a person outside Islam.
s.7087987b02e16e71: The Prophet peace be upon him called showing off the lesser shirk, in a report collected by Imam Ahmad. Swearing by other than Allah, and saying what Allah and so and so willed, belong to the same family. The point is not to make a believer anxious about every sentence, but to keep worship pointed in one direction.
s.52381f6c5e4fc832: Minor shirk · Lesser shirk · Shirk al-Asghar · Shirk khafi · Hidden shirk · Riya
s.e6fddfbe2a3ac6ac: Doubtful matters: the grey band between what is clearly lawful and what is clearly forbidden.
s.ac14ee4c38461862: The Prophet peace be upon him said the lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are unclear matters that many people do not know, and whoever guards against them has protected his religion and his honour, in Bukhari and Muslim. The same hadith ends by naming the heart as the organ that settles the body. Leaving the doubtful is wara', and it is personal caution rather than a ruling you impose on other people.
s.40dc076cd01b4696: Shubuhaat · Shubha · Shubhat · Mushtabihat · Doubtful matters · Grey area
s.189a30bdd954e3b3: Gratitude that shows: knowing the gift, saying so, and using it as its Giver would like.
s.ee995a51a2853b0b: The Qur'an promises increase to those who are grateful (Qur'an 14:7). Scholars describe shukr working in three places at once: the heart admits where the gift came from, the tongue says it, and the limbs do not use the gift against the One who gave it. The Prophet peace be upon him also said that whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah, in Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi.
s.9a7efa60279a0af2: Shukur · Shukran · Sukur · Shukr Allah · Shakir · Gratitude
s.fb96015a95de06e8: Truthfulness: that your words, your intentions and your actions all report the same thing.
s.467811b2b415e04c: The Qur'an tells the believers to be with the truthful (Qur'an 9:119), and the Prophet peace be upon him said truthfulness leads to righteousness and righteousness leads to Paradise, in Bukhari and Muslim. Writers on the heart use sidq more widely than honest speech: a truthful hope, a truthful repentance, a truthful claim to love Allah. In that sense its opposite is not only lying but posing.
s.b11b9f05297c2f2b: Sedq · Sidk · Sidiq · Siddiq · Sadiq · Truthfulness
s.d986bc4010bac9d2: The Lote Tree at the furthest limit, reached by the Prophet on the Night Journey.
s.ea62c49e3803e244: The Qur'an says he saw him at a second descent, by the Lote Tree of the utmost boundary, near which is the Garden of Refuge (Qur'an 53:13-15). Scholars describe it as the boundary past which the knowledge of creation does not go, so it marks a limit rather than a location. It appears in the accounts of the Night Journey, at the stage where the five daily prayers were given.
s.f9a017464b182000: Sidratul Muntaha · Sidra tul Muntaha · Sidrat ul Muntaha · Sidratul Muntahaa · Sidrah · Lote Tree
s.f1917373102058ad: The qualities of each letter: whispered or voiced, heavy or light, tense or flowing.
s.6068d443bf0b6065: Two letters can share one articulation point and still be different letters because their qualities differ, as with ta and da. Some qualities come in opposite pairs and some stand alone, like the whistle of sin or the roll of ra. Together with the makharij they are the two halves of pronouncing a letter correctly.
s.05d2725b84504d65: Sifat · Sifaat · Sifat al huruf · Sifaat ul huroof · Hams · Jahr
s.d84f837392715205: Sorcery: real in its effect, but powerless to harm anyone except by Allah's permission.
s.59919c0fecae6925: The word covers sorcery worked with the help of devils, and the Qur'an describes it plainly while making clear that it harms nobody except by Allah's permission (Qur'an 2:102). The Prophet peace be upon him was himself affected by it, in Bukhari and Muslim, and he recovered; he also named it among the seven destructive sins. Learning it or commissioning it is a grave matter, and the schools of law differ over the penalty for the one who practises it. The treatment is ruqya, the daily adhkar and ordinary medicine, never counter-magic.
s.23f6a086e0216978: Sehr · Sihir · Sahir · Sehir · Magic · Black magic
s.af1d1ced97ee53a3: The life story of the Prophet Muhammad, told in order, from birth to death.
s.ba44106134207db7: The root means to travel, so a sirah is the road a person walked. The oldest surviving account is Ibn Ishaq's, preserved in the edition of Ibn Hisham, alongside al-Waqidi and the Tabaqat of Ibn Sa'd. Sirah writers accepted material on a looser standard of proof than the hadith scholars did, so a story being famous in the sirah does not by itself make it authentic.
s.9102913dd53033ab: Seerah · Sira · Seera · Siera · Sirah Nabawiyyah · Seerat
s.1f756e6cc0fb779a: The bridge laid over Hell that everyone must cross, at speeds matching their deeds.
s.93cdd287b59101dd: It is described in the long hadith of intercession in Bukhari and Muslim: people pass over it like lightning, like the wind, like a running horse, or crawling, and some are seized along the way. The Qur'an speaks of every one of you coming to it (Qur'an 19:71), which many commentators read as this crossing. The same word in Surah al-Fatihah means the straight path in this life, a different sense of one root.
s.dd41553f345bf361: Siraat · Sirath · Sarat · As-Sirat · Pul Sirat · Pul-e-Sirat
s.1c785dae10f4d5c0: A twig used to clean the teeth, recommended before prayer, wudu, and on waking.
s.057a011dd3a56aeb: It is cut from the arak tree, softened at one end into bristles. The Prophet said that were it not a hardship, he would have ordered it before every prayer. It is a sunnah of cleanliness rather than a condition of anything, and a toothbrush achieves most of the same purpose for anyone who has no arak wood.
s.4dc0c7c0e69a87c6: Miswak · Meswak · Siwaak · Misvak · Arak stick · Salvadora persica
s.00c590d449f9d3be: Companionship: the people you sit with, treated in the sources as a cause of what you become.
s.3abb6c8e654152dc: The Prophet peace be upon him compared a good companion to a seller of musk and a bad one to a blacksmith's bellows, in Bukhari and Muslim, and said a person follows the way of his close friend, in Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi. Writers on the heart therefore treat the choice of company as an act with consequences rather than an accident. In Sufi usage suhbah also names the particular bond between a student and a teacher.
s.e0d6998143deee87: Suhba · Sohbet · Suhbat · Sohbat · Jalis · Companionship
s.fd56da15e3275dab: The meal eaten before dawn to begin a day of fasting.
s.e0804d89271f2f1b: The name comes from sahar, the last darkness before dawn. The Prophet said to eat it because there is blessing in it, and encouraged delaying it until close to the dawn. It is a sunnah rather than a condition, so a fast is still valid if a person sleeps through it.
s.2b50b09f7379898d: Sehri · Sahur · Suhoor · Sohour · Sahri · Sehri time
s.567ba3b0f44e14e6: The prostration, forehead and nose on the ground, done twice in every rak'ah.
s.fe07551bf2be05e9: Seven parts touch the ground: the forehead with the nose, the two palms, the two knees, and the toes of both feet. The Prophet said a servant is nearest to his Lord in sujud, and told us to make much supplication there. It is the posture the whole prayer is built around, not a formality between recitations.
s.498841a9f18cd71f: Sujood · Sajda · Sajdah · Sujuud · Sadjah · Sajood
s.6ee304d4f161872a: Two extra prostrations that repair a mistake made by forgetting during the prayer.
s.60b316561902833c: They cover adding a posture, leaving out a required part, or losing count. The Prophet said that when a person is unsure, he should settle on the lower number and make the two prostrations. The schools place them differently, before or after the closing salam depending on the kind of mistake, so follow what your local imam does rather than assuming an error.
s.6ae7cc90d8e10632: Sujud as-sahw · Sajda sahw · Sajdah sahw · Sujood sahw · prostration of forgetfulness · Sahw
s.560f73e2fc30fe28: A single prostration made when reciting or hearing one of the Qur'an's verses of prostration.
s.b567af22fcda6fb0: Copies of the Qur'an mark these verses in the margin. Depending on the school they are counted as eleven, fourteen or fifteen. It is one prostration, done inside or outside prayer, and it is recommended rather than required for most scholars. A related act is sujud ash-shukr, a prostration of thanks on receiving good news.
s.70ade48dd485fb23: Sajdah tilawah · Sujood tilawah · Sajda e tilawat · prostration of recitation · Tilawah sajda · recitation prostration
s.5c827b525ae8109c: A hadith book arranged by the chapters of fiqh, gathering the reports a jurist needs.
s.799b5f2c4ef6d066: The four Sunan among the six books are those of Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, and in its own way al-Tirmidhi. Unlike the two Sahihs they include weak reports, usually with a remark, because their purpose is to lay out the evidence on each legal question rather than to collect only what is sound. Reading them well means reading the author's comments, not only the texts.
s.84c539e48e726c62: Sunen · As-Sunan · Sunan books · Sunan Abi Dawud · Sunan Abu Dawood · Sunan al-Nasai
s.d63c167a986d363c: The Prophet's way in belief, worship and conduct, and the measure against which innovation is judged.
s.2d1af88dc63ac407: The word means a trodden path. In hadith study it covers what the Prophet peace be upon him said, did, and quietly approved; in fiqh it also names a recommended act; in creed it means the received way of the first generations, which is why the phrase Ahl al-Sunnah exists. Set against bid'ah, sunnah means the shape of the religion as it was handed over, rather than anyone's personal preference.
s.25779af8442cf502: Sunna · Sunnat · As-Sunnah · Sunnahs · Sunan · Way of the Prophet
s.8274881a2bc6a1bc: The regular voluntary prayers attached before or after the five obligatory ones.
s.22ec5e134663dd59: Twelve rak'ahs are reported as the standing pattern: two before Fajr, four before and two after Dhuhr, two after Maghrib, and two after Isha. The two before Fajr were the ones the Prophet never left. Any voluntary prayer outside this pattern is called nafl, and it carries no blame if missed.
s.83781930f572e322: Sunan rawatib · Rawatib · Ratibah · Sunnah muakkadah · Sunnat · Sunnah prayers
s.9207747bbdea1e51: The horn that is blown to end this world, and blown again to raise the dead.
s.7cabfe6e1eee04a8: The Qur'an says the horn is blown and everyone in the heavens and the earth falls dead except whom Allah wills, then it is blown a second time and they are standing, looking on (Qur'an 39:68). The angel entrusted with it is named Israfil in the hadith literature. Reports describe him holding it to his mouth, head inclined, waiting for the command.
s.5233a3901d2387ee: Soor · Sour · As-Sur · Nafkh as-Sur · The Trumpet · The Horn
s.f6983c94f61c5812: A chapter of the Qur'an; there are 114, arranged in the mushaf rather than by date of revelation.
s.f8cb0294847a379e: Each surah has a name, usually taken from a striking word inside it, and every surah except at-Tawbah opens with the basmalah. They range from al-Baqarah at 286 verses down to al-Kawthar at three. The order in the mushaf is not the order of revelation, so many of the short surahs at the end are among the earliest to come down.
s.c8720bfd13d572e7: Sura · Soorah · Surat · Suratul · Suwar · Sourate
s.d13512968df5eecc: Interpretation, and in a second sense the reality a statement finally turns out to refer to.
s.a72fedeb0f0eee29: Early scholars used ta'wil and tafsir almost interchangeably; Tabari's great commentary carries the word in its title. Later it came to mean moving a word away from its apparent sense on the strength of evidence, which is where much theological argument lives. In Shia and Sufi writing the word often carries a further sense, an inner meaning beneath the plain one, which Sunni scholars accept only where it does not cancel the plain meaning.
s.d33f19a6c0b9faa8: Tawil · Ta'weel · Taweel · Taawil · Tavil · Batin
s.1975479b3930e5ed: Discretionary punishment, set by a judge for offences that carry no fixed penalty.
s.47d59b8ca9e0f98a: The word means correction. It covers the vast majority of wrongdoing, from fraud and bribery to public nuisance, and it can be a warning, a fine, imprisonment or public rebuke. The judge weighs the person, the offence and the circumstances, and most jurists hold that ta'zir must stay below the level of a hadd. This flexible category, and not the hudud, is where classical Islamic criminal justice actually did its daily work.
s.9f61acb178aa7f4b: Tazir · Taazir · Tazirat · Tazeer · Taazeer · Tezir
s.48fa41f8f25a59da: Seeking blessing through a person, place or object, which scholars permit narrowly and dispute widely.
s.32616863ab8dc7d5: The Companions sought blessing through the person of the Prophet peace be upon him, his hair and the water left from his wudu, which is established in Bukhari and Muslim. Everyone agrees that the blessing itself comes from Allah alone. Scholars disagree about extending the practice after his death to graves, relics and living righteous people, some permitting it within limits, others treating it as a door that opens onto shirk. All sides agree that asking the object itself for anything is not tabarruk but worship of it.
s.112e13d48f6b33b6: Tabaruk · Tabaruck · Tabarruk bil-athar · Seeking blessing · Barakah from relics · Relics
s.9066e5f19ba4490b: The third generation: those who met the Followers, the last age the Prophet praised by name.
s.5f3450c77244e7d5: Malik ibn Anas, Sufyan ath-Thawri, al-Awza'i, Shu'bah and Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak stand in this layer. It is the generation in which the schools of law took shape and hadith began to be gathered into books rather than carried in memory alone. Together with the Companions and the Followers they make up the salaf, the three generations of praise.
s.cf03581971f21e47: Tabi at-Tabiin · Taba Tabieen · Atba at-Tabiin · Atbaa ut Tabieen · Tabe Tabaeen · Third generation
s.4ba694dbe40f5645: A Muslim of the generation after the Companions, who met a Companion but not the Prophet.
s.8ae098b2ef8c8500: The plural is tabi'un or tabi'in. They form the second layer in almost every chain, and figures like Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan al-Basri and Ibn Sirin belong here. Their own statements are called maqtu', and their reports about the Prophet without naming the Companion in between are called mursal.
s.7b4b60e58a18ca83: Tabii · Tabi · Tabi'in · Tabiin · Tabi'een · Tabieen
s.aacc69935d31f2f9: The second generation: Muslims who met Companions but never met the Prophet himself.
s.29f245b1fa86a1cb: They are the ones who received Islam warm from the hands that had held it, and they built the first schools of law and Qur'an teaching. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibn Sirin and Urwah ibn az-Zubayr belong here, and the Prophet named Uways al-Qarani the best of them without ever meeting him. The Prophet said the best of people are his generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them.
s.36cc468f12c084a9: Tabiun · Tabieen · Tabi'in · Tabiin · Tabaeen · Taabieen
s.08b590c938c0747f: The last expedition the Prophet led, a long march north in year nine that ended without battle.
s.3cbc1f35e7d9617f: It was called the army of hardship: high summer, scarce water, ripe harvests left behind, and a distant enemy. Uthman equipped a large part of it from his own wealth. No fighting took place. Its lasting story is the three Companions who simply failed to go and would not lie about why; the community was told to shun them for fifty nights until Surah at-Tawbah announced that Allah had turned to them, a passage that is really about honesty when a lie would have been easy.
s.75e71fa7b21b73b1: Battle of Tabuk · Ghazwat Tabuk · Jaysh al-Usrah · Army of Hardship · Tabook · Tebuk
s.fc6a9336ba2992bc: Slow reflection on the Qur'an, letting a verse work on you instead of passing over it.
s.8e0b292c92faa6ca: The root means to look at the far end of a thing, to follow it to its outcome. The Qur'an names this as the purpose of its revelation and asks more than once whether people reflect on it at all. Tadabbur is not tafsir: it needs no training, only attention, honesty, and enough of the meaning to know what you are reading.
s.49953f9379f8ad3d: Tadabur · Tadabbor · Tadabbur al-Quran · Tadabbur e Quran · reflection on the Quran · pondering the Quran
s.a3e344d653bd1e44: Wording a chain so that a gap or a weak teacher is hidden, without stating an outright lie.
s.051124b81d1674ea: The word comes from trading in dim light so the buyer cannot see the flaw. The classic form is a narrator saying from so and so about a man he met but did not hear this particular report from. Scholars listed the known mudallisin in ranks, and as a rule they do not accept such a narrator's report unless he says plainly that he heard it.
s.929f03bd9210b5d7: Tadlees · Tedlis · Mudallis · Mudallas · Mudalis · Tadleese
s.a95159db5c9135f1: The middle speed of recitation, sitting between the slow tartil and the quick hadr.
s.f5dfbd45085c23f3: It keeps every rule of tajwid fully in place while moving at a working pace. This is how most imams recite in tarawih and how most students revise. All three speeds are permitted; what is not permitted is speed that swallows letters.
s.37d252a0213e0d82: Tadweer · Tadwer · Tadwir recitation · medium speed recitation · middle pace · Tadwir Quran
s.c4fdfcff3bdaa331: Deliberate reflection on creation and on your own life, treated as an act of worship.
s.e22e85187e682dbe: The Qur'an describes people of understanding as those who remember Allah standing, sitting and lying on their sides, and who reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth (Qur'an 3:190-191). Scholars direct tafakkur outward at what has been made, and inward at one's own conduct, rather than at the nature of Allah Himself, which the mind cannot hold. A short honest stretch of thinking counts for more than a long distracted one.
s.21b9bb7d2304cd7b: Tafakur · Tefekkur · Tafkir · Tafakkur fi khalq · Reflection · Contemplation
s.85684163d3756135: Heavy and light pronunciation: some letters fill the mouth, others stay thin.
s.f93aee495f242cb3: Seven letters are always heavy, gathered by teachers in a mnemonic phrase, khussa daghtin qiz. Ra and the lam in the name Allah switch between heavy and light depending on the vowels around them, and alif simply follows whatever came before it. The distinction is not decorative: a heavy letter said thin can turn one word into a different word.
s.6525e115033b61c7: Tafkhim · Tafkheem · Tarqiq · Tarqeeq · Tafkheem tarqeeq · Isti'la
s.83eedb9f80ee1451: Explanation of the Qur'an: what a verse means, why it came, and what it asks of you.
s.be90a108ef12665a: The word means to uncover, the way you pull a cover off a thing. A tafsir works through the text verse by verse using the rest of the Qur'an, the Sunnah, the sayings of the Companions and the Arabic language. Tabari, Ibn Kathir, al-Qurtubi and al-Razi are among the best known, and they differ in focus, so reading one is not reading them all.
s.8f08d2cc8a4f5bea: Tafseer · Tefsir · Tafsear · Tafsire · Tafsirul Quran · Tafseer ul Quran
s.6581dc985264d2be: Tafsir built on transmitted reports, as against tafsir bi'r-ra'y, which reasons from language and principle.
s.3567ca2ed919cac8: Transmitted tafsir explains the Qur'an by the Qur'an, then by the Sunnah, then by the Companions and their students. Reasoned tafsir uses grammar, context and legal principle; it is praised when it is disciplined and condemned when it is a person reading their preferences into the text. Most of the great commentaries mix the two rather than holding to one.
s.e375ec1d3575c4d3: Tafsir bil Mathur · Tafsir bil-ma'thoor · Tafseer bil mathoor · Tafsir bir-ray · Tafsir bil ray · Tafsir bil rai
s.ebe57e1b25a4dced: Leaving the meaning of a difficult divine attribute to Allah, as opposed to interpreting it figuratively.
s.f037cf2ff4395495: When the texts describe Allah with a hand, a face, or a rising, scholars took two broad roads. Tafwid affirms the word and consigns its reality to Allah without explaining it. Ta'wil interprets it within what the Arabic allows, such as hand meaning power. Atharis lean to the first and Ash'aris and Maturidis often to the second, and each counts the other as Sunni.
s.653620e1d4f09f7f: Tafweed · Tafwidh · Tafwiz · Consigning the meaning · Leaving the meaning to Allah · Bila kayf
s.9bf3db6fb6895e9d: Voluntary prayer in the night, traditionally after sleeping and before dawn.
s.476c93a9808b5557: The root means to give up sleep. The Qur'an addresses the Prophet directly about it, and the last third of the night is its best time. There is no fixed number of rak'ahs; two is enough. Qiyam al-layl is a broader term for any prayer of the night, and in ordinary use the two words are treated as the same thing.
s.213ca87a8d6ab7f4: Tahajud · Tahujjud · Tahjud · Qiyam al-layl · Qiyamul layl · night prayer
s.e8d21bb3fdc4d501: Coming out of ihram, so that what was forbidden during it becomes permitted again.
s.69194d9921ef1123: In hajj it happens in two stages. The first comes after stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah and cutting the hair: normal clothes and perfume return, but intimacy does not. The second comes after tawaf al-ifadah and its sa'i, and lifts everything. In umrah there is only one, after the hair is cut.
s.b9708db0e9e47046: Tahalul · Tahallal · exiting ihram · leaving ihram · coming out of ihram · Tahallul awwal
s.040053204769b90e: Ritual purity, the state a person must be in before praying and, for most scholars, before touching the Qur'an.
s.0d8c1b2ce25c88ba: Books of fiqh almost always begin with taharah, because it is the gate to everything else. It has two sides: removing physical filth from the body, clothes and place of prayer, and lifting the ritual states that block worship. The Prophet called purification half of faith, and the Qur'an says Allah loves those who keep themselves pure.
s.7406f71b98561a7d: Tahara · Tahaarah · Tahaarat · Taharat · Tuhur · purity
s.728da43da8d0f4df: The rules for pronouncing the Qur'an correctly: each letter from its place, with its proper qualities.
s.0a03a94be0dae13d: The word means to do a thing well. In practice it covers articulation points, letter qualities, lengthening, merging, hiding, and where to stop. Scholars broadly agree that learning enough to avoid errors that change meaning is required of every reciter; how much of the finer detail is obligatory is debated, and a beginner is not sinful for reciting imperfectly while learning.
s.d85c80084bd52c5e: Tajweed · Tadjwid · Tajvid · Tajwed · Tejwid · Tajweed rules
s.0fca3d7f83b8c4b1: Cooperative insurance, built on mutual donation, offered as an alternative to conventional policies.
s.a3eb2c5bdd782b8d: Participants contribute to a shared fund on the basis of tabarru', donation, and the fund pays claims, while an operator manages it for a fee or an agreed share. It was designed to answer the objections scholars raise against conventional insurance, namely gharar, resemblance to gambling, and interest bearing reserves. Not every scholar accepts that the difference is substantive, and some hold conventional insurance permissible under necessity where no alternative is available.
s.e003d246af4dd638: Takafol · Takafful · Tekaful · Takaful insurance · Tabarru · Ta'awun
s.6a98890326b390f9: The opening "Allahu akbar" that begins the prayer and closes off everything outside it.
s.29605f11f5d5236b: Ihram here means entering a sanctified state, the same root as the pilgrim's ihram. Once you say the opening takbir, eating, speaking and turning away are no longer permitted until the closing salam. Smaller takbirs then mark each change of posture through the prayer.
s.4c835cf613f8d3ec: Takbir · Takbeer · Allahu akbar · Takbiratul ihram · opening takbir · Takbira
s.40805701adad9b9f: Declaring a specific Muslim to be a disbeliever, a ruling classical scholars fenced with heavy conditions.
s.34a8984d0ecfd477: Scholarship treats takfir as a judgement with conditions and impediments: ignorance, misreading, compulsion, and the absence of clear proof all block it. The Prophet peace be upon him warned that when a man calls his brother a disbeliever it returns to one of the two, in a report in Bukhari and Muslim. Saying that a statement is disbelief is not the same as saying the person who said it is a disbeliever, and the second was left to qualified scholars.
s.db98005650ff2650: Takfeer · Takfiri · Takfeeri · Declaring someone a kafir · Excommunication · Calling someone a disbeliever
s.835e1a08b099e0ce: Tracing a hadith to the books that recorded it, gathering its chains, and then grading it.
s.1b951872046b8ac8: The work has three steps: find where it was narrated, collect every route it came by, and weigh them together. It is the step most often skipped when a hadith is quoted online. A proper takhrij gives the source and the verdict, so a reader can check the claim instead of trusting whoever is quoting it.
s.5334fd75f29b7ff7: Takhreej · Tahrij · Takhrij al-hadith · Takhreej al-hadeeth · Tracing a hadith · Referencing hadith
s.88f8a6f22890dadc: Divorce pronounced by the husband, which Islamic law permits but treats as a last resort.
s.7699d3c05c8063de: The Qur'an gives it a whole surah and sets out a careful procedure: a single pronouncement, then a waiting period during which the couple may simply resume, with two further chances before the separation becomes final. Three pronouncements in one sitting are counted as three by the majority and as one by a minority, and this is among the oldest live disputes in fiqh. A woman who wishes to end a marriage uses khul' or asks a judge for faskh instead.
s.c0d37fe99050364f: Talak · Talaaq · Tallaq · Talq · Talaqe · Triple talaq
s.f1c4f2c8c98a6ac6: The pilgrim's answering call, beginning labbayk Allahumma labbayk, here I am, my Lord, here I am.
s.3a8897ac98af9bd2: It continues: no partner have You, here I am, all praise and favour are Yours, and the dominion, You have no partner. It is said on entering ihram and repeated on the road, aloud by men and quietly by women. It is an answer to the summons the Qur'an says Ibrahim was told to proclaim. On umrah pilgrims stop when they begin the tawaf; on hajj the talbiyah continues until the stoning on the tenth.
s.e8f4116b71b9c019: Talbiya · Labbaik · Labbayk · Labbaik Allahumma labbaik · Talbeeyah · Telbiye
s.9efdf9f864707bee: One of the three ways to perform hajj: umrah first, then leaving ihram, then hajj from Makkah.
s.c4e057c49d9ba312: In tamattu' you complete umrah, come out of ihram and wait, then enter ihram again for hajj on the eighth. In qiran you hold both in a single unbroken ihram, and in ifrad you perform hajj alone. Tamattu' and qiran require a hady; ifrad does not. The schools differ over which is best, and tamattu' is what most pilgrims on organised trips perform.
s.1687f2f932a09583: Tamattu · Tamatu · Temettu · Qiran · Qiraan · Ifrad
s.f4796e1362a5ac21: An amulet worn for protection, whose ruling depends on what has been put inside it.
s.6f430bcf7b808869: Amulets containing the names of jinn, unknown words or symbols are forbidden by agreement, and the Prophet peace be upon him warned that whoever hangs an amulet has been left to it, in reports collected by Ahmad and Tirmidhi. Amulets containing Qur'an are where scholars part company: Ibn Mas'ud and many after him prohibited them without distinction, while Abdullah ibn Amr and a number of Malikis and Shafi'is allowed the Qur'anic kind. Both sides agree the protection is from Allah, not from the paper.
s.2fd9ab914bb3abc3: Tameemah · Tamima · Tamaim · Taweez · Tawiz · Ta'wiz
s.5a4c9f3d52cbf717: Following a qualified scholar's ruling without knowing the underlying evidence yourself.
s.2c5ba5aefb6d72d4: It is what most Muslims do most of the time, and the Qur'an tells those who do not know to ask those who do. Scholars differ over its limits: some hold a layperson should commit to one school for coherence, others allow asking any trustworthy scholar, and all agree taqlid is not followed against a clear text one actually knows. The word is also used critically, for copying without thought, which is a different matter from consulting an expert.
s.154b94bcb856975a: Taqleed · Taklid · Taqlead · Taqliid · Muqallid · following a scholar
s.01e445b5be7bbc0f: Trimming the hair rather than shaving it, the alternative way to leave ihram.
s.24e41b318a936c07: Most schools require a little to be taken from all around the head rather than a single snip from one place. It is the option chosen by women, and by men who wish to keep hair for a shave at the end of a hajj that follows soon after. Both halq and taqsir close the rites of umrah, and no further trimming is needed after that.
s.9b9f56961deb7328: Taqseer · Taksir · Taqsir hair · trimming hair · cutting hair in umrah · Tasqir
s.61a2077cf5619c62: An alert, careful awareness of Allah that keeps a person away from what harms them.
s.7a66bac7c415b421: The root means to guard or to shield, and carries the sense of putting something between yourself and danger. The Qur'an calls it the best provision for the journey (Qur'an 2:197), and the Prophet peace be upon him pointed to his chest three times and said taqwa is here, in a report collected by Muslim. It is not fear alone, and it is not a personality type. It is caution kept awake.
s.bcb8f47dff63f3e3: Taqwah · Takwa · Taqwaa · Taqua · Tuqa · Takva
s.81195cc39773a5c5: The night prayer of Ramadan, prayed in congregation after Isha through the month.
s.3d865b725fc5fa48: The name comes from the pauses for rest taken after every four rak'ahs. The number differs by custom and school: twenty rak'ahs became the settled practice of most schools and thirty six the old practice of Madinah, while many mosques pray eight, following reports of the Prophet's own night prayer. The number is not the point of the argument it is often made into; both are within the tradition.
s.74982487e6f90a01: Taraweeh · Tarawee · Taravih · Salat at-tarawih · Ramadan night prayer · Terawih
s.c918bac0f9c6229a: A Sufi order: a lineage with a shaykh, a set litany, and a method for training students.
s.b30b6c0023432a0a: The word means path. Well known orders include the Qadiriyyah, the Naqshbandiyyah, the Shadhiliyyah and the Chishtiyyah, each with its own wird and manners. Belonging to one has never been a requirement in Islam, and scholars differ sharply about the orders as institutions, some treating them as a school of character, others objecting to particular practices found within them. The word is not used in this sense outside Sufi circles.
s.066d2ed97cc56a33: Tariqa · Tareeqa · Tarika · Tariqat · Turuq · Sufi order
s.b750484032ebada6: A translation of the Qur'an, properly called a translation of the meanings rather than the Qur'an itself.
s.84493c7ec8709064: No translation carries the Arabic wording, and every translator has already made interpretive choices, so a translation is really a compressed tafsir. This is why prayer is recited in Arabic; Abu Hanifah is reported to have allowed reciting the meaning in prayer, his two main students allowed it only for someone genuinely unable, and he is reported to have come round to their view. A translated volume is also not given the same rulings as a mushaf.
s.caaec10c460dea5a: Tarjuma · Tarjama · Tarjumah · Tarjumatul Quran · translation of the Quran · Quran translation
s.fad7257af68deb30: Reciting slowly and distinctly, giving every letter its right, as the Qur'an itself instructs.
s.f7aef5178907dca9: The command is direct: and recite the Qur'an with tartil. Ali is reported to have explained it as giving the letters their due and knowing where to stop. It was the Prophet's own pace, and it is the one to use if you want to understand what you are saying.
s.1a5b57a7b03630f5: Tarteel · Tartil Quran · Tarateel · Tartil recitation · slow recitation · measured recitation
s.c2228a2fa1c84cb5: The Islamic tradition of inner purification, called Sufism in English, and read very differently by different scholars.
s.f7f41460bf98b6f2: At its origin the word names the science of the heart: sincerity, remembrance, character and struggle against the self, as taught by early figures such as al-Junayd and later organised by al-Ghazali. Over the centuries it also grew orders, practices and claims that other scholars judged to be innovations, and opinion today runs from full acceptance to full rejection, with many holding the content sound wherever it stays inside the Book and the Sunnah. When you meet the word it helps to ask which is meant: the subject matter, or a particular order and what it does.
s.6cd1f2471f453175: Tasawuf · Tassawuf · Tasavvuf · Soofism · Sufism · Sufi
s.1e24399a254b1d04: Declaring Allah free of every imperfection, most often in the words subhan Allah.
s.da4ec8118d558773: The Prophet peace be upon him said two phrases are light on the tongue and heavy on the scale, subhan Allah wa bihamdih and subhan Allah al-azim, in Bukhari and Muslim, and he taught the counts said before sleeping. He counted on his fingers and told the women to do the same, since the fingers will be asked to testify, in Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi. Counting with beads was not the practice of his time; most later scholars allowed it as a tool, while some regarded it as an unwarranted addition.
s.3e794811fcdb8623: Tasbeeh · Tesbih · Tasbi · Tasbih Fatimah · Subhanallah · Subhan Allah
s.3885985910b15d97: The words said while sitting in prayer, testifying to faith and greeting the Prophet.
s.fd50fc3e18e73bec: The name comes from shahadah, testimony, because the words contain the declaration of faith. It is said in the sitting after the second rak'ah and again at the end of the prayer, where salawat on the Prophet is added before the closing salam. Several wordings are authentically reported, and mosques in different regions use different ones; all of them are sound.
s.3699ef854e50269f: Tashahud · Tashhahud · At-tahiyyat · Attahiyat · Tahiyyat · Tahiyat
s.851ec2cfe17cc67d: Likening Allah to His creation, which the Qur'an rules out with the words: there is nothing like Him.
s.1198ad700545f9da: Tashbih is imagining Allah as a bigger, stronger version of something you have already seen. Its mirror error is ta'til, emptying His names and attributes of any real meaning. Sunni creed walks between the two: He is real, He is described, and He is not comparable (Qur'an 42:11).
s.a009fd6bd519c7d9: Tashbeeh · Tajsim · Tamthil · Anthropomorphism · Likening God to creation · Tashbih wa Tajsim
s.f450daf59114ff8b: The closing greeting of peace, turned to the right then the left, that ends the prayer.
s.4d8dfc37476b3311: You say as-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah while turning the face to the right shoulder, then repeat it to the left. Until the taslim you are still in prayer and its restrictions apply. Some schools treat only the first salam as obligatory and the second as recommended.
s.caa143866c68f284: Tasleem · Salam · Salaam · Assalamu alaykum in prayer · ending the prayer · Taslim in salah
s.90197f4d79ebd447: Humility: knowing your size, without pretending to be smaller than you are.
s.3895dbf514e4d22f: The Prophet peace be upon him said nobody humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him, in Muslim, and the Qur'an describes the servants of the Most Merciful as those who walk on the earth gently (Qur'an 25:63). Scholars define it as accepting the truth from whoever brings it, and not seeing yourself as above anyone. Performed modesty, staged so that people will admire it, belongs with riya rather than with tawadu'.
s.9a89de44ad91506e: Tawaduh · Tawadhu · Tawaduu · Tevazu · Tawadhu' · Humility
s.c4709079235b148b: Circling the Kaaba seven times, keeping it on your left, starting and ending at the Black Stone.
s.b5a598725a07a50c: The Qur'an commands circling the Ancient House. Most schools require the pilgrim to be in a state of purity, and Hanafis count a tawaf made without wudu as valid but owing a dam. Each circuit begins and ends at the corner of the Black Stone. Hajj has up to three: tawaf al-qudum on arrival, tawaf al-ifadah after Arafah which is a pillar of the hajj, and tawaf al-wada as a farewell before leaving Makkah. There is no obligation to touch or kiss the stone; most pilgrims simply point to it.
s.aeb4c76f30eb2fb1: Tawaaf · Tawwaf · Tavaf · Tauf · circumambulation · circling the Kaaba
s.457664ca7757fc3c: Relying on Allah for the outcome while still doing the work that leads to it.
s.e168c50a834a7160: The Qur'an says whoever relies on Allah, He is enough for him (Qur'an 65:3), and it also tells the Prophet peace be upon him to consult, then decide, then rely (Qur'an 3:159). When a man asked whether to leave his camel loose and trust Allah, he was told to tie it and then trust, in a report collected by Tirmidhi. Tawakkul is the state of the heart after you have done what you can, not a reason to do nothing.
s.b6c59052e9b5827c: Tawakul · Tawakkal · Tawaqul · Tevekkul · Tawakkul alallah · Reliance on Allah
s.6d08f4f4508453e2: Approaching Allah through a means, such as His names, your own good deeds, or a living person's du'a.
s.26d7ebb413b0585a: All schools agree on three forms: by Allah's names and attributes, by your own righteous deeds, and by asking a living righteous person to pray for you, the last shown in the hadith of the blind man and in Umar asking al-Abbas to pray for rain. They differ over tawassul by the person or rank of a prophet or saint, especially after death. Many Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i and Sufi scholars permit it as a form of asking Allah, while Hanbali and Salafi scholarship generally rejects it as a door to worse. All sides agree that asking the dead to grant something themselves is not tawassul at all but shirk.
s.5dea88f4c761cc46: Tawasul · Tawassal · Tawwasul · Tawassul bil anbiya · Seeking a means · Intermediary
s.1d472f1a22a0eb80: Turning back to Allah from a sin: stopping it, regretting it, and resolving not to return.
s.0d46b2b08672a1aa: The Qur'an calls for a sincere turning, tawbatan nasuha (Qur'an 66:8). Scholars list the conditions as leaving the sin, regretting it, resolving not to repeat it, and, where a person's right was taken, returning it or seeking their pardon. The Prophet peace be upon him said every child of Adam errs, and the best of those who err are those who repent, in a report collected by Tirmidhi. Falling again does not cancel the earlier repentance; it calls for another one.
s.d566b9297b390be7: Tawba · Tauba · Taubah · Touba · Tobah · Tawbah nasuha
s.45320b1e26daf940: The belief that Allah is one, without partner, without equal, and alone deserving of worship.
s.51da1a4539121793: The word means to make one, or to declare one. Surah al-Ikhlas states it in four short lines: He is One, the Eternal Refuge, He does not beget and was not begotten, and there is nothing comparable to Him (Qur'an 112). Tawhid is not only the claim that one God exists. It is that only He is worshipped.
s.70ae1be2c3a3ae6c: Tawheed · Tauhid · Towhid · Tevhid · Tawhiid · Tauheed
s.52cbb87311f3e45d: Oneness of lordship: that Allah alone creates, owns, sustains and controls everything that exists.
s.779c7bcd4aa75b17: This is the belief that there is one Creator running one universe, and the Qur'an notes that even the idolaters of Makkah admitted this much when asked who made the heavens and the earth. That is why it is not, by itself, enough to make someone a Muslim. The three part division of tawhid is a teaching framework, used widely since Ibn Taymiyyah; some scholars prefer a two part arrangement, and the difference is about how to teach it rather than what is true.
s.9e8eb98e181187bc: Rububiyyah · Ruboobiyyah · Rububiya · Tawheed ar-Rububiyyah · Tawhid Rububiyya · Oneness of Lordship
s.9a8957f653134470: Oneness of worship: that prayer, vows, sacrifice, hope and fear are directed to Allah alone.
s.56b7dcbaf3e93ae4: This is the part the messengers were sent with, and the part people have always argued over. To believe Allah made you is one thing; to bring every act of worship to Him and to no one else is another. Its exact opposite is shirk.
s.773496170d7d5669: Uluhiyyah · Uloohiyyah · Ilahiyyah · Tawhid al-Ibadah · Tawheed al-Uluhiyyah · Oneness of worship
s.510adc41959de007: Purification with clean earth instead of water, when water is unavailable or would cause harm.
s.5802f24c2faef9ca: You strike clean ground or dust with the palms and wipe the face and the hands. The Qur'an permits it for the traveller, the ill, and anyone who cannot find water. It stands in for both wudu and ghusl, and it ends the moment water becomes usable again. It is a real concession, not a lesser or shameful substitute.
s.3423da1bf8751341: Tayamum · Tayammom · Teyemmum · Tayammun · dry ablution · dry wudu
s.297889fc0dd2acf2: The purification of the self: the work of clearing the heart of what spoils it.
s.bea066bae163d008: The Qur'an says the one who purifies the soul has succeeded (Qur'an 91:9), and lists purifying people among the tasks the Prophet peace be upon him was sent with (Qur'an 62:2). The subject covers both halves of the job: removing what is blameworthy, such as envy and arrogance, and planting what is praiseworthy, such as sincerity and gratitude. It is a discipline with a syllabus, not a mood, and it belongs to every Muslim rather than to one group.
s.b43a6e855a724b73: Tazkiya · Tazkiah · Tazkiyat al-nafs · Tazkiyah al-nafs · Tazkiat · Tazkiyya
s.7c97ff62c732f170: A trustworthy narrator: upright in character and accurate in memory, the two conditions held together.
s.c843235b4fabd01d: Uprightness without accuracy gives you a sincere man who misremembers. Accuracy without uprightness gives you a sharp man who lies. Only both together make a thiqah. Ranks below it include saduq, meaning truthful but slightly less precise, and layyin, meaning soft or weak.
s.6edc3a3bc6eb9705: Thiqa · Siqah · Siqa · Tiqah · Thiqaat · Thiqat
s.ee06c00cc3ef50aa: Reciting the Qur'an aloud, following its words closely rather than merely reading over them.
s.e990a0f5963d2adb: The root carries the sense of following, one word behind another, which is why the term implies obedience as well as recitation. The Qur'an praises those who recite it as it deserves to be recited. In practice tilawah is done with wudu where possible, at a measured pace, opening with the isti'adhah.
s.909293b0fb63941e: Tilawa · Tilaawah · Tilawat · Telawa · Tilawah Quran · Tilawat e Quran
s.5f79eef4e855510a: Whether wudu is needed to hold a copy of the Qur'an; the four schools say yes, a minority disagrees.
s.e1e777ca0c029df8: The four Sunni schools require purity to touch the mushaf itself, citing a verse in Surah al-Waqi'ah and the Prophet's letter to the people of Yemen; Ibn Hazm and others read that verse as speaking about the angels instead. Reciting from memory without wudu is agreed to be fine. Most contemporary scholars hold that a phone or tablet is not a mushaf, so the ruling does not extend to reading from a screen.
s.80930a0b50553b4d: Mass al-Mushaf · Massul Mushaf · touching the Quran · touching Quran without wudu · holding the Quran · Quran without ablution
s.d86cc0151e173ee7: The beginner's tajwid poem students memorise, alongside al-Jazariyyah and, for the readings, ash-Shatibiyyah.
s.333360e22254e620: Tuhfat al-Atfal, by al-Jamzuri, covers the rules of nun sakinah, meem sakinah and madd in about sixty lines of verse. Al-Jazariyyah, by Ibn al-Jazari, goes further into the articulation points and qualities of the letters. Ash-Shatibiyyah is the long poem behind the seven readings, and students normally reach it only after the first two are secure.
s.529334974754164d: Tuhfatul Atfal · Tuhfa · Tohfatul Atfal · Jazariyyah · Al-Jazariyyah · Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah
s.086be54bc4d69831: The animal sacrificed on Eid al-Adha and the days after it, in remembrance of Ibrahim.
s.0f6088d59d113f7b: It is offered after the Eid prayer on the tenth of Dhul Hijjah and through the days of tashriq. The Hanafis hold it obligatory on whoever has the means; the other three schools call it a confirmed sunnah. The meat is customarily divided in three, for the household, for relatives and neighbours, and for the poor, though that division is a practice rather than a fixed ruling. It is not the same as the hady, the sacrifice a pilgrim offers as part of Hajj.
s.1a6ea364fcc24f5a: Qurbani · Qurban · Korban · Kurban · Adahi · Dhabihah of Eid
s.4d0319d109413db3: The battle at the mountain outside Madinah where an early Muslim advantage collapsed into losses.
s.4d66a30d775cfd0f: The Prophet posted archers on a hill and told them not to leave it whatever happened. When Quraysh broke and the Muslims began collecting spoils, most of the archers came down, and Khalid ibn al-Walid's cavalry came round the open flank. Around seventy Companions were killed, including Hamzah, and the Prophet himself was wounded. Surah Al Imran discusses the day at length, without softening it, which is part of why the Qur'an's honesty about its own community is striking.
s.8327f2716cb987f3: Battle of Uhud · Ghazwat Uhud · Jang e Uhud · Ohod · Uhad · Mount Uhud
s.81aa5bbe7284ec88: The science of testing reports about the Prophet, deciding which are sound and which are not.
s.58b277fd98a34a37: Every report is judged from two sides: the chain of people who passed it on, and the wording they carried. The classic handbook is the Muqaddimah of Ibn al-Salah, and Ibn Hajar's short Nukhbat al-Fikar is the summary students still memorise.
s.6faa6319c7257413: Uloom al-Hadith · Ilm al-Hadith · Mustalah al-Hadith · Mustalah · Hadith sciences · Ulum ul Hadith
s.18f0e6b64092bacc: The family of disciplines that study how the Qur'an was revealed, collected, recited, read and interpreted.
s.020d3b0d6468db8f: It covers revelation and its occasions, Makkan and Madinan passages, the canonical readings, abrogation, the clear and the ambiguous, and the rules of interpretation. It is the map you are meant to have before opening a work of tafsir. The two classic reference works are al-Zarkashi's al-Burhan and al-Suyuti's al-Itqan.
s.99f53349a1888107: Uloom al-Quran · Ulum ul Quran · Ulumul Quran · Uloom ul Quran · Quranic sciences · sciences of the Quran
s.765b0b508002130a: The Umayyad caliph whose short reign is remembered as a return to the way of the Rashidun.
s.d1e6b7cd5c7acf4f: He ruled about two and a half years from the ninety ninth year of the Hijrah. He returned property his family had taken, stopped the cursing of Ali from the pulpits, lightened taxes on new Muslims, and lived so plainly that his own household noticed the change first. He is also the caliph who ordered hadith to be gathered and written down systematically, which is why so much survives. Many scholars call him the fifth of the rightly guided caliphs.
s.c52bf2fafd348680: Umar bin Abdul Aziz · Omar ibn Abdul Aziz · Umar II · Omar bin Abdulaziz · Umar ibn Abdulaziz · Fifth rightly guided caliph
s.5bdc4f0551b7e6b3: The second caliph, called al-Faruq, under whom the Muslim state expanded enormously.
s.cbe33fe95edb9eeb: He had set out to kill the Prophet and accepted Islam on the road, after hearing Surah Ta Ha in his sister's house. As caliph for about ten years he took Syria, Egypt, Iraq and Persia, and built the machinery of a state: a treasury, a stipend register, provincial governors held to account, and the Hijri calendar. Several rulings were revealed in line with opinions he had voiced. He walked Madinah at night without guards, and was stabbed while leading fajr.
s.7657f4ad715cf363: Umar · Omar · Umar bin Khattab · Umar al-Faruq · Omar ibn al-Khattab · Hazrat Umar
s.1e5c9048029af386: The whole body of Muslims, across every land and century, treated as one community.
s.f3c4a334a9258956: The root is umm, mother, so an ummah is a people gathered around one origin. The Qur'an calls this community a middle nation and says your ummah is one ummah, and it uses the same word for other nations, for a stretch of time, and once for Ibrahim alone, a single man called a whole community. In practice the word carries a duty: what happens to Muslims elsewhere is not other people's news.
s.c8eb06d3d694e84d: Umma · Ummat · Ummah Muslimah · Umat · Oomah · Ummet
s.6e39d2e6add9347c: The Prophet's wives, whom the Qur'an names as mothers to every believer.
s.f68cc114dbf088c2: Surah al-Ahzab says his wives are their mothers, and in the same surah forbids anyone to marry them after him. He was married to eleven women across his life, nine of whom survived him; for twenty five years, until he was fifty, he was married to Khadijah alone. Several were widows, and the marriages knitted together tribes that had been enemies. Aishah and Umm Salamah in particular transmitted a large part of what is known about his private practice.
s.e9fda067637f5d7d: Ummahat ul Muminin · Ummahatul Mumineen · Mothers of the Believers · Ummahat al-Mumineen · Ummuhat al-Muminin · Wives of the Prophet
s.c0cd0c2669801010: The lesser pilgrimage: ihram, tawaf, sa'i and cutting the hair, and it may be done any time of year.
s.404151c04a77c3de: It shares its rites with hajj but has no Arafah, no Mina and no fixed date. It takes a few hours rather than several days. Shafi'is and Hanbalis hold umrah obligatory once in a lifetime; Hanafis and Malikis call it a confirmed sunnah. Performing it in Ramadan is described in a well known hadith as equal in reward to a hajj, which does not remove the obligation of hajj itself.
s.6ecb313e256643a4: Umra · Omra · Umrah pilgrimage · Umre · lesser pilgrimage · minor pilgrimage
s.b6ebf1c91cb17a6f: The science of how rulings are derived: which sources count, and how they are read.
s.5d02b9cf51a4b9ed: Literally the roots of fiqh. Where fiqh gives you the answer, usul al-fiqh gives you the method: the four sources agreed by the Sunni schools are the Qur'an, the Sunnah, ijma' and qiyas, together with rules for language, abrogation and conflicting evidence. Al-Shafi'i's Risalah is the earliest surviving book devoted to the subject.
s.55c69b95b8a52fbf: Usul al fiqh · Usool al-Fiqh · Usul ul Fiqh · Usul fiqh · Osul al-Fiqh · Usul
s.98efef1817372232: The third caliph, called Dhun-Nurayn, who fixed the Qur'an in one agreed written text.
s.aaf0d54936f4aaf7: The title means possessor of two lights, because he married two of the Prophet's daughters in turn. He was wealthy and gave heavily: he bought the well of Rumah for the people of Madinah and equipped much of the army of Tabuk. His great act as caliph was to standardise the mushaf, sending official copies to the provinces when he saw reciters disputing over readings. Rebels besieged his house and killed him while he was reading the Qur'an; he refused to let anyone fight for him.
s.90bb4f627d582c84: Uthman · Usman · Osman · Othman · Uthman bin Affan · Hazrat Usman
s.3f0e0e9c4e63e8f2: Revelation: Allah's speech conveyed to a prophet, directly, from behind a veil, or through an angel.
s.52dfe21ec0ada4bc: The Qur'an describes exactly those three modes (Qur'an 42:51), and says the Prophet peace be upon him did not speak from desire, but that it was revelation revealed (Qur'an 53:3-4). Revelation of this kind came to prophets only, and it ended with the death of the last of them. Nothing after him, however sincere or however true it feels, carries the same authority. Where the Qur'an uses the same verb of the bee or of the mother of Musa, scholars read inspiration rather than prophecy.
s.8216786d4a4c7a5b: Wahi · Wahee · Wahyi · Vahiy · Wahyu · Revelation
s.9b0dafa097e67d76: Obligatory. In the Hanafi school, a step below fard, resting on slightly weaker evidence.
s.836db4d96ee546eb: For Malikis, Shafi'is and Hanbalis, wajib and fard are two words for one category. Hanafis separate them: the witr prayer and the sacrifice at Eid al-Adha are wajib rather than fard, so neglecting them is sinful while denying them is not disbelief. In hajj the distinction has a practical edge, since a missed wajib can be repaired by a sacrifice while a missed pillar cannot.
s.4789e399f93b6ba3: Waajib · Wajeb · Vacip · Vajib · Wujub · Wajibat
s.20090ef7d84a783d: The male relative who contracts a woman's marriage on her behalf, usually her father.
s.60842aff5adfdba5: Malikis, Shafi'is and Hanbalis hold a marriage invalid without one, citing the report that there is no marriage without a wali. Hanafis hold that an adult woman may contract her own marriage, though her guardian may object to a plainly unsuitable match. Whether a father may marry off a virgin daughter without her word is the oldest dispute here: Hanafis say no, the other three allowed it under conditions, Ibn Taymiyyah rejected it. The Prophet annulled the marriage of a woman whose father had contracted it against her will.
s.1e23cdf7e7eff9c1: Wali · Walee · Waliy · Vali · Veli · Wali nikah
s.5b6ad77de85ccb9b: The wedding feast held after the marriage, and a strongly confirmed sunnah on the groom.
s.2bb9dc2943c2f5af: The Prophet told 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf to hold one even if only with a single sheep, and he taught that answering the invitation is a duty on those invited unless they have an excuse. Most scholars hold the walimah itself is a confirmed sunnah rather than obligatory. He also warned against a feast to which only the rich are invited and the poor are turned away, which is the part most often forgotten.

s.b2caaace6e98fcb4: A permanent charitable endowment: property held forever so that its income keeps serving a purpose.
s.35e068cd28f2d207: 'Umar asked the Prophet about land he had acquired at Khaybar and was told to hold the property itself and give away its produce, which became the model. Once made, a waqf cannot be sold, given away or inherited, and it is administered for its stated beneficiaries, whether a mosque, a school, a well or a family. Historically waqf funded most of the Muslim world's hospitals, libraries and colleges, and it remains the fullest form of ongoing charity.

s.44c3b85c8e0fe412: The familiar marks come from a system worked out by later scholars rather than from revelation: meem means stop, la means do not stop here, jeem means you may, and paired sets of three dots mean stop at one of the two but not both. Stopping in the wrong place can break the sense of a sentence, which is why the marks were added at all. The same word waqf also means a charitable endowment, an entirely separate subject.

s.6d745c8aa0614d60: The Prophet peace be upon him said the lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters, and whoever avoids them has protected his religion, in Bukhari and Muslim. He also said to leave what makes you uneasy for what does not, in a report collected by Tirmidhi. Wara' works one step further out than taqwa, in the grey band. It becomes a problem only when it turns into suspicion of everything and everyone.

s.682201851450324b: Uthman ibn Sa'id, nicknamed Warsh, took it from Nafi al-Madani, and it travelled west with the scholars of the Maghrib. Set beside Hafs it lengthens certain vowels further, handles some hamzahs more softly, and tilts some fathas towards a kasra. Nafi's other transmitter is Qalun, whose reading is used in Libya and parts of Tunisia.

s.88e088dd46e2c10f: The Qur'an commands: seek the means of nearness to Him (Qur'an 5:35), which the commentators explain as obedience and whatever brings a servant close. The word is also the name of a rank in Paradise which the Prophet peace be upon him said belongs to one servant only, and which he taught his community to ask for on his behalf after the call to prayer. The two meanings share a root and are often mixed up in argument.

s.bad2d0eb195b7711: The Qur'an mentions it before the inheritance shares, and debts are settled before both. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas asked about leaving his whole estate to charity and was told a third, and that even a third is a great deal. A wasiyyah cannot be made in favour of someone who already inherits, since their share is fixed by revelation, so it is used for non heirs, for charity, and for burial and guardianship instructions.

s.ff17869d1836c75b: Whispering: unwanted thoughts thrown at the heart, whether by Shaytan or by the mind itself.
s.7f1d6e9b5f901451: The last surah of the Qur'an names the whisperer who whispers in the chests of people (Qur'an 114:4-5). The Prophet peace be upon him said Allah has pardoned this community for what their souls whisper as long as they do not act on it or speak it, in Bukhari and Muslim, and he taught that a person struck by doubts about creation should say I believe in Allah and move on. Distressing repetitive doubt about wudu, prayer or belief is a recognised condition, and treating it as a medical matter as well as a spiritual one is not a failure of faith.

s.3bc2a3c58e5153df: A personal daily portion of remembrance or recitation that a person keeps to.
s.d97a3e601622fb46: The word means a turn at a watering place. In practice a wird is a small fixed amount, a page of Qur'an, a number of salawat, a set of adhkar, repeated every day at the same point. The principle behind it is the prophetic teaching that the deeds most loved by Allah are the constant ones, even if small. Sufi orders assign a specific wird through a shaykh; outside that setting a person simply chooses their own and keeps it.

s.7e2448671a35b565: Witr means odd, as opposed to even. It is prayed any time after Isha until dawn, and the Prophet told his companions to make it the last prayer of their night. Hanafis classify it as wajib, close to obligatory; the other three schools call it a confirmed sunnah. Someone who intends to pray tahajjud usually delays witr until after it.

s.6094c04b3c4e8ccd: The four acts are named directly in the Qur'an, and the Prophet added rinsing the mouth and nose, washing the hands first, and doing each part three times. Wudu is broken by using the toilet, by passing wind, and by deep sleep; it is not broken by touching an animal or by ordinary dirt. One wudu lasts for as many prayers as you like until something breaks it.

s.36ffcb48bf3db8ca: The Prophet said the hajj is Arafah. A pilgrim who reaches any part of the plain within its window has performed it, whether standing, sitting or asleep, and one who misses it has missed the hajj that year. The majority date the window from midday until dawn of the next day; Hanbalis start it at dawn on the ninth. The day is spent in supplication rather than in any set ritual.

s.45a2de957b8de537: The Qur'an tells the story of the barrier of iron and molten copper (Qur'an 18:94-98) and says that when they are released they will swarm down from every height (Qur'an 21:96). Scholars have guessed for centuries about who and where they are; the honest answer is that the texts describe a time, not a place on a map. Their release is one of the ten major signs.

s.492a31d4e252692e: The Qur'an mentions degrees that scholars read as a ladder: the knowledge of certainty and the eye of certainty (Qur'an 102:5-7), and the truth of certainty (Qur'an 56:95). The difference is like being told about a fire, then seeing it, then feeling its heat. The Qur'an also says worship your Lord until certainty comes to you (Qur'an 15:99), which the commentators explain as death.

s.7b43383c8e9b4f82: The yearly obligatory share of qualifying wealth, normally 2.5 percent, given to those entitled to it.
s.7e38e9fb628579e5: The word carries both purification and growth. Zakat is the third pillar, and the Qur'an names it beside the prayer again and again. It is due on savings, gold, silver and trade goods held for a lunar year above the nisab, at one fortieth of their value, while crops, livestock and mined wealth have their own rates. It is a debt owed to specific people, not a donation the giver may direct wherever they wish.

s.8046839b05336589: A small measure of staple food given for every household member before the Eid al-Fitr prayer.
s.0a4776b164a0fc03: The Prophet made it obligatory on every Muslim, young and old, free and owned, as a purification for the fasting person and food for the poor. The measure is one sa', roughly two and a half to three kilograms of the local staple. Hanafis permit paying its value in money, which most charities now do; the other schools generally require the food itself. Given after the Eid prayer it counts as ordinary charity, so it is paid early.

s.e0744dc74c261249: Zakat on wealth: normally one fortieth of qualifying savings held for a full lunar year.
s.3e7dba101615ee46: It is distinguished from zakat al-fitr, the small fixed measure of food given per person at the end of Ramadan. It falls due on cash, gold, silver, trade stock and recoverable debts once they pass the nisab and a lunar year has turned, while crops, livestock and mined wealth have their own rates and no year requirement. Your home, personal belongings and the tools of your trade are exempt. Scholars differ over pensions, shares, and gold jewellery in regular use.

s.c8da70dd49ee07f3: Left in a dry valley with her baby, Hajar ran seven times between two hills looking for help, and water broke open at the child's feet. The name is said to come from her words as she banked the sand to hold it in. The well was lost for centuries and rediscovered by Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's grandfather. s.678679a442cfb056: There are two Eids and no more: one at the end of a month of hunger, one on the morning after the pilgrims stand at Arafah. Almost everything they ask of you is the same, and the parts that differ are the parts people most often get wrong. This room leads with whichever is nearest and keeps the other one open beside it, all year, because the question of how the prayer works does not wait for the week it is due.
s.9618ec93235e98d5: There are two Eids and only two. Everything else a Muslim community celebrates is a custom, which is not a criticism, only an accurate description. This one room holds both of them, because most of what they ask of you is identical: the same takbir, the same washing and the same best clothes, the same two rak’ahs with no call to prayer, the same sermon afterwards, the same instruction to take a different road home, the same absolute prohibition on fasting the day itself.
s.c521f28963da3583: The page leads with whichever Eid is nearest. The other one stays exactly where it is, fully readable, all year, because the question of how the Eid prayer works does not only occur to people in the week it is due.

The verse does not say every year, and it does not say everyone. It says whoever is able, once.

s.715b1b6630d96648: Whoever cannot find or afford one fasts three days during the Hajj and seven after returning home. The schools differ on when the three may be fasted: many allow them from the entry into ihram for Umrah, most prefer the seventh, eighth and ninth, and if they are missed the Hanafis and others discuss whether the days of Tashriq, the three days that follow the sacrifice, may be used. If you expect to fast rather than slaughter, settle this with a scholar before you travel, not on the ninth.
s.a923c887e1ba5761: the three days may be fasted after entering ihram for Umrah and before the day of Arafah. That they may not be delayed past the day of Arafah is the well known view, and it is stated here more crisply than the madhhab holds it: Hanafi authorities differ among themselves over what is owed by one who lets those days pass, and they do not all answer the same way.
s.32bb35f62bae8d94: the standard summary is that they may be fasted from the entry into ihram for Hajj, and that the Shafi’is do not permit them in the days of Tashriq in the strongest view. The Maliki half of that line is thin, and their books are reported with more than one starting point, so a Maliki should settle it with a scholar of his own school.
s.bdae188c54fd703e: permits fasting them in the days of Tashriq for one who did not fast them before, on the strength of the report of Aisha and Ibn Umar.

s.3b5e72e4265ccad6: Ihram is the most misunderstood word in this whole chapter. It is not the towels. It is a state you enter with an intention at a fixed boundary, and the cloth is only its uniform. Once you are in it, a list of ordinary lawful things becomes unlawful to you until you are released, and some of them cost you a sacrifice if you break them.
s.54d3a4bede22b3ec: Five gates set on a ring around Makkah, one for each direction of arrival, each with an arrow pointing inward to the House.

s.9772f7ea3812c598: Dhul Hulayfah, for the people of Madinah and anyone coming through it, about four hundred and fifty kilometres out and the furthest of them, known today as Abyar Ali. Al-Juhfah, for the people of Sham, Egypt and the west, north of Makkah, with Rabigh used in its place today. Qarn al-Manazil, for the people of Najd, to the east, known today as as-Sayl al-Kabir. Yalamlam, for the people of Yemen, to the south, used also by many arriving from South and Southeast Asia. And Dhat Irq, for the people of Iraq, to the north east.

s.e57acf2a41df62dc: In practice this means changing into the ihram garments at home or at the airport you depart from, and making the intention and beginning the talbiyah, the pilgrim’s call, when the crew announces the miqat or roughly half an hour before landing, whichever comes first. Making the intention early is safe. Making it late is not.
s.0bbc391e1784cef4: Whoever crosses his miqat without ihram and then intends Hajj or Umrah must go back to the line and enter from there. If he does not go back, the four schools hold a dam, a sacrifice, is due from him, and his Hajj is still valid. Note the word intending: someone travelling to Jeddah for work, with no intention of Umrah, is not bound by the line at the moment he crosses it.

s.12dbfc53815e1115: hold that if he returns to the miqat and enters ihram there, the sacrifice falls away; the Shafi’is hold similarly, and the difference between them lies in whether the return must be before he begins any rite.

s.afff3d7088b661f6: Ihram is an intention, made in the heart, to enter the rites. The cloth is not the ihram. A man wrapped in two white sheets who has not intended anything is a man in two sheets. s.afe22a1ec1090948: The prohibitions that carry an expiation
s.37246a8882729f22: These are the ones with a price attached. Removing hair from the head or body, and by agreement the cutting of nails. Applying perfume to the body or clothes, including scented soap, scented cream and scented deodorant. For a man, wearing anything stitched or shaped to a limb: shirt, trousers, underwear, socks, and covering the head with anything resting on it. For a woman, the niqab and gloves. Touching a spouse with desire. Hunting land game, or helping someone else hunt it.
s.8f0fb7a66eecd2e4: Hunting has its own expiation, named in the Qur’an: a like animal from the livestock, judged by two just men, or the feeding of the poor, or an equivalent in fasting. Sea game stays lawful throughout. And note the boundary: buying meat that someone else lawfully slaughtered is not hunting.
s.8fe51288f248a59e: do not shave until the sacrifice reaches its place; the threefold expiation
s.3a4fde6600935024: the narration of Ka’b ibn Ujrah, whose head was covered in lice, given the three choices of fasting, feeding or a sacrifice
s.9e3bfc9ac9f5e9a8: the expiation for hunting while in ihram
s.087403825bd429f0: the game of the sea is lawful to you
s.80d0a14769149551: What breaks the Hajj outright, and what only wounds it
s.f61c164e6468376c: There is one prohibition in a class of its own. Sexual intercourse before the first release on the tenth invalidates the Hajj itself, by the agreement of the four schools. The pilgrim must complete the rites anyway, must repeat the Hajj the following year, and owes a badanah, a camel. It is worth being honest that this ruling is built on the judgements of the Companions, chiefly Umar, Ali and Ibn Abbas, rather than on an explicit prophetic text, and that the schools accepted it as settled.
s.1c345db0d5817176: Intercourse after the first release but before tawaf al-ifadah is different: the Hajj is not invalidated, an expiation is due, and one re-enters ihram from outside the sanctuary to complete the remaining tawaf. The details differ by school and this is a scholar’s question.
s.0a176d83171e2255: At the other end of the list sit the prohibitions with no material expiation at all: arguing, quarrelling, obscene speech and sin, named in the Qur’an as the things that hollow out a Hajj from inside. There is no sheep for these. There is repentance, and there is the person you were rude to, whose forgiveness you now have to go and ask for.
s.d0b68c9e20581910: agree that intercourse before the first release invalidates the Hajj, that it must still be completed, and that it must be repeated.
s.73694c2de3e72edb: the expiation in that case is a sheep if it occurred after standing at Arafah, and a camel if before it.
s.9902bd93f6ab4a15: a camel is due, with detail on who bears it if both spouses were in ihram.
s.d3b02ddf0fd5f635: the boundary of intimacy, set by Allah and not to be approached
s.e360ba44e10f423e: The famous differences inside the list
s.40cbb86581b297c7: Three of these come up on nearly every journey, and knowing that the schools differ will save you an argument in a tent.
s.e49b6d9ff2402891: Third, and most useful of all: what happens if you break a prohibition by accident, out of forgetfulness or not knowing. This is not a small technicality. It happens to almost everyone, usually with scented soap.
s.7662a35838f638be: the standard summary is that the expiation is due even from one who forgot or did not know, because it repairs a right of the rite rather than punishing a sin. That summary flattens the Maliki position, which carries recognised exceptions and excuses in a number of these cases, so a Maliki should not read this line as the whole of his school.
s.78e1d10b8e3abf7d: excuse the forgetful and the genuinely ignorant in several of these, notably perfume, clothing and covering the head, holding no expiation is due once the thing is removed at once.

s.607b463c60661c36: What stays lawful, and gets asked about anyway
s.ec794f81187f7dcb: Washing, showering and swimming. Unscented soap. Changing your ihram cloths, and washing them. Wearing a watch, glasses, a ring, a hearing aid, a money belt around the waist, and a bag over the shoulder. Sheltering under an umbrella, a tent, or the roof of a bus. Covering the face for a man, in the view of the majority. Killing harmful creatures. Scratching your head gently, even if a hair or two falls without intent.
s.4109cd2f6e8a982d: The two that trip people most often: sandals or flip flops that leave the ankle bone and the top of the foot open are fine, and a wide elastic belt with pockets is fine because it is a belt, not a garment shaped to the body. When in doubt, the test for a man is simple. Is this sewn or shaped to fit a limb, and is it being worn the way that limb’s clothing is worn.
s.440deb35feb8632b: A grid of nine drawn marks, each struck through, naming what is forbidden while in ihram and what it costs.
s.5e9946652e4930a7: The standard summary is that the Hanafis and Malikis hold the expiation due even from one who forgot or did not know, though the Maliki position carries recognised exceptions that the summary flattens. The Shafi’is and Hanbalis excuse the forgetful in several of these, provided he stops the moment he realises.
s.bf62dece998c6310: Washing, unscented soap, a watch, glasses, a ring, a belt with a pocket, an umbrella and sandals that leave the ankle open all stay lawful throughout.
s.841b0c2f5730e8e9: Qur’an 2:196, 5:95 and Bukhari, the narration of Ka’b ibn Ujrah.
s.ac9ecd38bbc9300e: The gold word under each mark is its price. A fidyah is your choice of three: fast three days, feed six poor people, or slaughter a sheep, and it is owed without sin by anyone who broke the rule out of genuine need. Only one thing in this grid invalidates the Hajj itself, and one of them belongs to the sanctuary rather than to your ihram.
s.6001dd8c5f293b1a: Umrah is four steps and a few hours, and it is the best possible rehearsal for Hajj, because tawaf and sa’i return in the middle of the fifth day when you are tired. Learn them properly here, once, calmly, and the tenth of Dhul Hijjah will be far easier.
s.50f8c5e57f85c87b: Seven loops spiralling outward around a central cube, with the corner of the Black Stone marked as the start and the finish of every circuit.
s.f33b75bd81f98b53: anticlockwise, the House on your left
s.7e03272962246a33: every circuit starts and ends here
s.be33edb6db557c28: Kiss the Stone if there is space. If not, face it, raise your right hand, say Allahu akbar, and keep walking. A sunnah never sits on top of harming someone.
s.4dfbc1376f935bed: The Hijr, the low curved wall, is part of the House. Your circuit goes outside it, not through it.
s.cef96e1fe74a5bb9: Ramal, the brisk short step in the first three circuits, and idtiba’, the bared right shoulder, are for men only, and both drop away in a crowd.
s.eed53ce3dd108809: The spiral is drawn open so you can count the seven. In the mosque they lie on top of each other, which is exactly why pilgrims lose count. If you do, build on the smaller number you are certain of and complete it. Nothing in tawaf has fixed words except the takbir at the Stone and the verse said between the Yamani corner and the Black Stone.
s.a496b26a79173b58: Wash, wear the two cloths if you are a man or your ordinary modest dress if you are a woman, and at the miqat intend Umrah in your heart. Then begin the talbiyah and keep saying it all the way to Makkah.
s.7074809cbdda4266: The schools count this differently in their lists, though nothing practical changes: the Hanafis call ihram a shart, a condition of the Umrah, with tawaf as its pillar. The others count ihram itself among the pillars. Either way, without it you have not begun.
s.fa5d47d237aa1108: no crossing of the miqat without ihram for one intending the rites
s.afc9a3e4da78bd0e: Two: entering the Haram, and the first sight
s.a8414e7167b0d60f: Enter with the right foot and say the du’a for entering any mosque. Then the Kaaba comes into view, and this is the moment everyone has been told to prepare a special supplication for.
s.46d2b510119e67ca: the narration on entering the mosque: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy
s.052751069d34f3a0: Tawaf is circling the Kaaba seven times, anticlockwise, with the House on your left. It starts at the corner of al-Hajar al-Aswad, the Black Stone, and it ends there. Every circuit is one full pass from that corner back to it. Counting matters more than speed; lose count and you build on the lower number you are certain of.
s.5cdf8a7c1522c2d2: The conditions are: covering what must be covered, being inside the mosque, keeping the House on your left, staying outside the Hijr, that low curved wall, because it is part of the House itself as Aisha was told, and beginning and ending at the Stone. Purity is the one condition the schools split on, and it matters enormously for women, so it has its own note below.
s.1834b0c8d0395fae: For men only, in a tawaf that will be followed by sa’i: ramal, walking briskly with short quick steps, in the first three circuits, and idtiba’, passing the upper cloth under the right armpit so the right shoulder is bare, for the whole tawaf. Both are sunnah, both drop away in a crowd where they would harm someone, and neither applies to women.
s.b4e09f3884e237ce: Nothing else in the tawaf has fixed words. There is no prescribed du’a for the first circuit or the fourth. Say what you want, recite Qur’an, remember Allah, ask for your mother.
s.1a17476680f04f28: purity from both minor and major impurity is a condition of tawaf; a tawaf performed without wudu is not valid.
s.4cd9e9655e05d58b: purity is wajib, an obligation, not a condition; a tawaf performed without wudu is valid and a sacrifice repairs it, and one performed in a state of major impurity requires a badanah and is better repeated.

s.d1622e15644c3b8f: Pray two units behind Maqam Ibrahim, the standing place of Ibrahim, if there is space, reciting al-Kafirun in the first and al-Ikhlas in the second, as Jabir described. If the area is packed, and it usually is, pray them anywhere in the mosque. Do not push through a tawaf to reach the Maqam. There is no requirement to be near it.
